content:
University of California, Irvine researchers have mapped approximately 8 million cells in deep regions of the human brain, identifying 60 distinct cell types and describing how they form cellular communities.  

The resulting reference is intended to support investigations of brain systems affected by Parkinson’s disease, Huntington’s disease and other neurological and psychiatric disorders.
summary: Researchers at the University of California, Irvine mapped approximately 8 million cells in deep regions of the human brain, identifying 60 distinct types and how they form cellular communities. The map provides a foundational reference for studying brain systems affected by Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, and other neurological and psychiatric disorders.

title: MIT researchers unveil AI copilot that improves topology optimization designs
content:
MIT researchers have developed a new AI “copilot” system designed to make algorithmic structural design more collaborative and accessible. Published in an open-access paper in Communications Engineering, the system addresses the limitations of current topology optimization techniques, which often require significant computation and time, leaving users with only the final design to review. This “black box” nature makes it difficult for engineers to trust that the resulting structures are sound or practical to build. By integrating human feedback during the generation process, the new approach aims to produce designs that are both high-performing and manufacturable.

The system utilizes machine learning to identify specific regions of an evolving algorithmic design where human input is most likely needed. To train this model, the researchers created a synthetic dataset containing probable human feedback on thousands of designs, critiquing aspects such as aesthetics, performance criteria, and manufacturability. Lead author Dat Ha, a recent MIT civil and environmental engineering doctoral student and current structural designer at LeMessurier, noted that the goal was to leverage human cognitive abilities to solve complex design problems in a way that is more practical for industry. The approach allows designers to maintain agency and control over the design process as it unfolds.

In demonstrations, the human-in-the-loop approach improved manufacturability and linear buckling load by 39 percent while adding only 15 seconds to the total design time compared to all-algorithmic methods. Senior author Josephine Carstensen, an MIT associate professor of civil and environmental engineering, explained that previous attempts to add human judgment slowed the process dramatically, but this new system maintains efficiency. The researchers believe this method could make topology optimization more widely adopted, particularly in fields like buildings and bridges, where engineers have historically been skeptical of computer-generated designs that may feature impractical elements, such as multiple beam connections at a single point.

Currently, the system allows users to modify identified regions by making them thicker or thinner, with plans to add other modification options in future versions. The team, which includes Ferdous Alam, Markus Buehler, Faez Ahmed, and Carstensen, views the approach as complementary to purely algorithmic methods. Carstensen stated that disciplines with abundant computational resources can continue using AI-only approaches, while those requiring human decision-making can utilize this collaborative model. The work was supported in part by the MathWorks Engineering Fellowship Fund, TATA Steel, and the MIT Generative AI Impact Consortium.
summary: MIT researchers developed a human‑in‑the‑loop AI copilot for topology optimization that lets designers give feedback on regions while the algorithm generates a structure. The system improved manufacturability and linear buckling load by 39 % and added only 15 seconds to total design time compared to fully algorithmic approaches.

A recent study examined more than 2,500 men to explore the relationship between protein source and testosterone levels.  

Researchers found that higher intake of animal protein, especially from dairy, was associated with lower testosterone, whereas plant protein intake correlated with higher testosterone.  

The results suggest that everyday dietary choices may influence male hormone levels, prompting further investigation into the link between protein source and testosterone.

content:
Researchers at Brown University have overcome a major obstacle to creating ultra‑low‑power computer chips that could help slash the energy demands of AI.

Their breakthrough eliminates a long‑standing “dead layer” problem that causes promising materials to stop working when made extremely thin.

Remarkably, the new technique not only preserves the materials’ electrical and magnetic properties at nearly atomic thicknesses but also gives them enhanced magnetic capabilities.

In mice, removing this protein caused muscles to struggle with self-repair and led to a dramatic acceleration in the progression of muscular dystrophy.

Distinct patterns of brain activity were linked to these difficulties and could even predict certain math‑related abilities.

title: Global Rebound of Mangrove Forests Begins 2010, Expanding in Asia, Australia, South America
content:
Research published in Science indicates that global mangrove forests have experienced a significant rebound since 2010, reversing decades of decline. Scientists analyzed Landsat imagery collected between 1984 and 2023 to assess changes in mangrove extent and canopy density. The study found that while mangroves lost nearly 3,000 square kilometers (1,200 square miles) between 1984 and 2010, the trend shifted to an increase of nearly 2,000 square kilometers (770 square miles) after 2010. This expansion was led by growth in Asia, Australia, and South America, with many forests now exhibiting denser, more closed canopies than in 2010, particularly in South America.

Zhen Zhang, an environmental scientist at Tulane University, noted that these are the first global mangrove maps covering such a long period. According to Zhang, approximately two-thirds of the recent expansion resulted from mangroves colonizing new areas, while the remaining third came from restoration and regrowth in degraded areas. The study highlights that mangrove trees, which average about 13 meters (43 feet) in height, store up to four times as much carbon as taller inland tropical forests. They also protect coastal communities from erosion and storm surges, while their root systems provide habitat for fish, shrimp, and crabs.

Burma (Myanmar) serves as a notable example of this reversal. The country had lost mangroves rapidly in the 1980s and 1990s due to agriculture, aquaculture, and firewood harvesting. However, the trend reversed around 2010, with mangrove area expanding in many locations. The authors attribute this turnaround to increased awareness and restoration efforts following the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, strengthened legal protections, and high rates of sedimentation that created new mudflats for colonization. Landsat images of Burma’s Myeik District show mangroves replacing rice fields in Palaw Township, with regeneration occurring in abandoned fields south of the village of Kyauktaung.

Despite these gains, challenges remain. Burma lost 28.6 percent of its mangrove area between the 1980s and 2010, though the area has grown by about 10 percent since then. In other regions, losses have outweighed gains; substantial losses in the Niger Delta have reduced mangrove area in West and Central Africa since 2010, while tropical cyclones have caused widespread degradation in North America and southern Africa. Conversely, sediment deposition around the mouth of the Amazon River and in northern Australia has allowed mangroves to colonize new mudflats, contributing to steady increases since the 1990s. Additionally, warming temperatures and fewer freezes have enabled mangroves to expand into previously too-cold areas, including the southeastern U.S.

Zhang cautioned that the global successes observed over the past decade should not lead to complacency. He emphasized that conservation efforts and slowing deforestation can yield significant positive impacts when combined with natural expansion and regeneration. The study underscores the importance of continued protection for these ecosystems, which play a vital role in climate resilience and coastal stability.
summary: Scientists using Landsat imagery from 1984 to 2023 found that mangrove area fell by nearly 3,000 km² between 1984 and 2010, then increased by almost 2,000 km² after 2010. The rebound was driven by expansion in Asia, Australia, and South America, with many forests now denser and healthier than in 2010.

title: RealtimeVAD reduces end‑of‑speech latency by 110 ms at cost of false positives
content:
A developer has released RealtimeVAD, a voice activity detection tool designed to reduce end-of-speech latency in local voice assistant pipelines. The project addresses the lag in the Silero VAD model’s speech-off signal by incorporating a 10 ms energy detector with a threshold that adapts to ambient noise. While this approach increases the number of false positives, the developer notes that this is acceptable for their speculative generation pipeline, as incorrect triggers can be quickly aborted if the user continues speaking.

Benchmarking the solution against approximately 3,200 turns from assistant logs revealed an initial latency improvement of 110 ms. Following a necessary fix for handling quiet speech, the current latency reduction stands at 100 ms. The developer has made the code public, including a benchmark script, and is seeking feedback from users who test the tool on their own data.
summary: The author implemented a 10 ms energy detector that trades false positives for earlier end‑of‑speech detection, achieving a 110 ms latency improvement. The solution was benchmarked on ~3200 assistant turns and is publicly available with a benchmark script.

summary: Nvidia employees posted an internal petition urging the board to consider bringing back former CEO Jensen Huang. The post has drawn more than 1,600 comments, the majority of which support reinstating him.
author: Wired

title: Xbox announces Wolfenstein 3 sequel from MachineGames
content: A screenshot from Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus. It's been nearly a decade since Bethesda's MachineGames released Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus in 2017, and now Xbox is ready to announce a sequel from the studio. Wolfenstein 3 was officially announced today, just days after Bethesda also confirmed that the next Elder Scrolls game will be called The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. In a post, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced the name and a photo of a script. "Looking forward to sharing more," she said. MachineGames also announced the game in a post, saying the game is "in production" and sharing a photo from a motion-capture session. IGN reports that Brian Bloom (who plays protagonist William …
summary: Xbox announced Wolfenstein 3, a sequel to 2017’s Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma posted the title and a script photo, and MachineGames said the game is in production and shared a motion‑capture image.
author: The Verge

title: Donald Trump urges former Apple CEO Tim Cook to lead Nvidia after Jensen Huang resigns
content:
Jensen Huang announced his resignation as Nvidia’s chief executive this morning amid reports of personal affairs, including an alleged connection to a Chinese spy. The company’s chief financial officer has assumed interim leadership while the board searches for a permanent replacement.

President Donald Trump responded on Truth Social, stating that the only suitable successor is former Apple chief executive Tim Cook. Cook, who left Apple’s CEO post on September 1 and moved to an executive‑chairman role, was singled out by Trump as his preferred candidate to lead the chipmaker.
summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO and the CFO is acting as interim chief executive. President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that former Apple CEO Tim Cook, now executive chairman, should become Nvidia's next CEO.
author: The Verge

title: Jensen Huang resigns, raising doubts about Nvidia's open source AI support
content: Jensen Huang’s resignation has prompted scrutiny of Nvidia’s dedication to open‑source AI. Observers note the company’s recent Hugging Face acquisition, its development of open‑weight models and its public stance against AI restrictions, all of which are now being re‑examined as Nvidia undergoes a leadership transition.
summary: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia. His resignation raises questions about Nvidia’s commitment to open source AI, including its Hugging Face acquisition, open-weight models and advocacy against restrictions, as the company undergoes a leadership transition.
author: TechCrunch

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid affair, raising questions on AI chip supply
content:
Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair have intensified scrutiny on Nvidia’s corporate contracts and supply chains. The article examines whether the AI economy can endure without Huang, who is described as central to the world’s second-most valuable company. It questions the broader global implications of any potential decline in Nvidia’s fortunes.

Nvidia’s high valuation relies on its design and sale of advanced graphics processing units (GPUs), which are essential for the AI economy. According to the source, AI models like ChatGPT and Claude cannot be trained or run without these chips.
summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s CEO, resigned after an affair, drawing attention to the company’s corporate contracts and supply chains. Nvidia, the world’s second‑most valuable company, relies on its advanced AI GPUs that power models such as ChatGPT and Claude.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Eight dead, others trapped after NYC building collapse; man says his kids among trapped
content: A building collapse in New York City left eight people dead and left additional individuals trapped in the rubble, according to local media. One resident, Anderson Velez, said he was at work when his wife called to tell him that their two children, aged 2 and 7, were among those trapped.
summary: Eight people were killed and others remain trapped after a building collapsed in New York City. Anderson Velez said his wife called him at work to tell him their two children, ages 2 and 7, were among those trapped.
author: Euronews

title: Doomsday study's 13 November 2026 world‑end prediction proven false
content: According to a study, the end of the world was meant to arrive on 13 November. That sounds dramatic and would seem urgent, if the study were not already "outdated", yet it is still intriguing.
summary: A study predicted the world would end on 13 November 2026. The prediction has been shown to be incorrect.
author: Euronews

title: Senator Chris Van Hollen announces challenge to Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer
content: U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen has announced a challenge to Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer, becoming the first Democrat to openly contest Schumer’s bid for the position. Van Hollen’s challenge is backed by a segment of the party’s more vocal progressive members.
summary: Chris Van Hollen, who has support from some of the more vocal progressives within the Democratic party, is the first to openly challenge long-term Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer's bid.
author: Euronews

title: Zelensky cautions Europe about US‑Russia talks on new security arrangement
content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky cautioned European leaders on Thursday to be wary of ongoing discussions between the United States and Russia concerning a new continental security arrangement. He highlighted that, prior to Russia’s 2022 invasion, the Kremlin had issued an ultimatum to NATO demanding the withdrawal of forces from eastern Europe and a halt to the alliance’s expansion. The warning was reported by FRANCE 24’s Caroline Baum.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned European leaders on Thursday to be wary of United States‑Russia discussions about a new security arrangement for the continent. He noted that before launching the war in 2022 the Kremlin delivered an ultimatum to NATO demanding withdrawal of forces from eastern Europe and a stop to accepting new members.
author: France 24

title: Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital in Gaza kills six, including surgeon
content: Israeli fire killed 11 people in Gaza on Thursday, including six in the early‑day bombing of Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza, health officials said, marking the deadliest single strike since Israel’s elections last month. FRANCE 24’s Mark Owen interviewed Dr Goher Rahbour, a surgeon at Nasser Hospital.
summary: Israeli fire killed 11 people in Gaza on Thursday, including six in the bombing of Nasser Hospital in south Gaza, health officials said. The strike was the deadliest single attack since Israel's elections last month, and France 24's Mark Owen interviewed surgeon Dr Goher Rahbour from the hospital.
author: France 24

title: Victor Casallo welcomes Pope Leo at Antonio Ruiz de Montoya University, citing Peru
content:
François Picard welcomed Victor Casallo, director of the Department of Philosophical and Theological Studies at Antonio Ruiz de Montoya University, to discuss the role of Pope Leo—identified as the first American‑born pontiff—in Peru. Casallo emphasized that Leo’s identity cannot be understood solely through his Chicago origins.

According to Casallo, the pope’s decades of pastoral work in Peru unfolded amid political instability, terrorism, state violence and deep social inequality. He said these experiences have shaped a religious outlook characterized by cultural openness, solidarity with the marginalized and a close familiarity with human suffering.

Casallo also noted a broader societal challenge, observing that “we tend to see the other person not as someone who holds a different opinion, but as an enemy.” He suggested that Leo’s background may offer a perspective for a polarized nation seeking dialogue and healing.
summary: François Picard welcomed Victor Casallo, Director of the Department of Philosophical and Theological Studies at Antonio Ruiz de Montoya University. Casallo said Pope Leo’s decades of pastoral work in Peru amid political instability, terrorism, state violence and social inequality shaped his outlook of cultural openness, solidarity with the marginalized and understanding of human suffering.
author: France 24

title: Zelensky and Kushner say Europe to join next Russia-Ukraine talks
content: Jared Kushner said on Thursday that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to broaden the upcoming round of negotiations to incorporate European nations, a development confirmed by President Volodymyr Zelensky and Kushner. He added that Washington is pursuing what he described as the war’s “largest prisoner exchange.”
summary: Zelensky and Jared Kushner said Russia and Ukraine have agreed to expand the next round of talks to include European nations. Kushner said Washington is working toward what he called the war's largest prisoner exchange.
author: France 24

title: Haitian security forces retake national football stadium after two years of gang control
content: Haitian security forces regained control of the country’s main football stadium on Thursday, ending two years of gang occupation, and Salvadoran troops have assumed security duties at the venue. The operation coincides with El Salvador’s deployment of 2,000 soldiers to Haiti after an ambush that left four of its troops missing.
summary: Haitian security forces regained control of the country's main football stadium on Thursday after two years under gang control. Salvadoran troops are now handling security at the venue as El Salvador deploys 2,000 soldiers to Haiti following an ambush that left four of its troops missing.
author: France 24

title: Pope Leo XIV meets six abuse victims in Peru, urges Church to make amends
content: Pope Leo XIV met six victims of clerical abuse in Peru on Thursday, among them individuals linked to the disbanded Sodalitium Christianae Vitae. The US‑born pontiff called on the Catholic Church to make amends to survivors and to strengthen protections against abuse as he returned to the country where he served for nearly two decades.
summary: Pope Leo XIV met six victims of clerical abuse in Peru on Thursday, including people linked to the disbanded Sodalitium Christianae Vitae. The US-born pontiff urged the Catholic Church to make amends to survivors and strengthen protections against abuse as he returned to the country where he served for nearly two decades.
author: France 24

title: Microsoft works to fix 10‑hour global Outlook and Teams outage
content: Microsoft reported that Outlook and Teams experienced a global disruption lasting roughly 10 hours on Thursday. The outage, which affected businesses and government agencies worldwide, was attributed by the company to elevated infrastructure loads. Microsoft said it was working to restore the affected services.
summary: Outlook and Teams were down for about 10 hours on Thursday, affecting businesses and government agencies worldwide. Microsoft said the disruption was caused by elevated infrastructure loads and that it was working to restore the services.
author: France 24

title: EU leaders debate who will represent Europe in Ukraine‑Russia peace talks
content: EU leaders are debating which representative to send to upcoming Ukraine‑Russia peace talks. A U.S. envoy, after meeting with President Putin, indicated that a European seat at the negotiating table now appears likely, but the identity of the European delegate remains undecided.
summary: A seat at the table for Europe now appears likely following comments by a US envoy who just held talks with Putin. But who will take that seat remains unclear.
author: DW World

title: Iranian boxer death row inmate Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani wins Magnitsky award
content:
Iranian boxing champion and coach Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, a political prisoner sentenced to death three times, was awarded the Magnitsky humanitarian prize for outstanding human‑rights activism. The ceremony took place in London on Thursday night, where Vafaei Sani accepted the award on behalf of “the generation that is paying the price of freedom with their lives” and declared he will “never surrender” and will not bow before oppression.

Vafaei Sani is listed among seven athletes in Iran who face execution, and his receipt of the Magnitsky award highlights his status as a boxer on death row who continues to advocate for human rights.
summary: Iranian boxer death row inmate Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani wins Magnitsky award.
author: Guardian World

title: Over 60% of Germany's female soldiers report harassment, minister vows zero tolerance
content:
More than 60 % of Germany’s female soldiers report experiencing harassment or abuse, according to a new study. The research, the first comprehensive examination of its kind on the Bundeswehr, was conducted by the Centre for Military History and Social Sciences in Potsdam and released this week.

Defence Minister announced that the extent of sexual misconduct uncovered by the study is “unacceptable” and pledged a zero‑tolerance approach to sexual abuse within the armed forces. The military is also working to attract new recruits amid rising global threats, hoping reforms will improve its image and recruitment prospects.
summary: A study by the Centre for Military History and Social Sciences in Potsdam found that more than 60% of Germany’s female soldiers reported harassment or abuse. Germany’s defence minister said the level of sexual misconduct is unacceptable and pledged a zero‑tolerance approach as the Bundeswehr seeks new recruits.
author: Guardian World

title: Study finds children’s wood‑burning exposure may match traffic exhaust
content: New research across six European towns and cities measured air quality in buildings where children spend much of their time, including schools, sports centres and homes. The scientists focused on polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH), a group of pollutants released when fuels are burned. Their findings show the highest levels of cancer‑related PAH pollutants in cities with widespread wood heating, and suggest that children’s exposure to emissions from home wood‑burning could be as significant as exposure to traffic exhaust.
summary: Researchers measured polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) in schools, sports centres and homes across six European towns and cities. They found that children’s exposure to wood‑burning emissions could be as significant as exposure to traffic exhaust, with the highest cancer‑related PAH levels in cities where wood heating is widespread.
author: Guardian World

title: Australian teen William survives six nights lost in Victoria's bush
content:
A 17‑year‑old boy identified only as William survived nearly a week after becoming lost in dense bushland in Victoria’s east. He had been dropped off by his mother on a weekend to camp with a friend last Friday.

William said the nights were “pretty cold” and that he “honestly didn’t think” he would survive. While awaiting rescue, he sang John Denver’s “Take Me Home, Country Roads” to keep hope alive during the long, solitary nights.
summary: William, 17, was dropped off by his mother to camp with a friend in Victoria’s east last Friday and became lost in dense bushland. He survived six nights, enduring cold nights, drinking creek water, eating chips and singing “Take Me Home, Country Roads” while hoping for rescue.
author: Guardian World

title: Microsoft Outlook and Teams outage hits Australian schools and government services
content: Government services and schools impacted by Outlook and Teams issue as company says fix not ‘taking as expected’ Microsoft outage – live updates Microsoft struggles to fix huge outage affecting Outlook and Teams Australian schools, courts and government services have been hurled back in time to how business used to be done after a global Microsoft outage caused emails and online meetings to go dark. Australians began reporting issues with Microsoft 365 – which includes Outlook and Teams – just before 5am AEST on Friday, according to Down Detector. The problem appeared to peak at 9.22am with more than 5,500 reports of problems, including trouble opening and sending emails, before reports began to dip.
summary: Microsoft Outlook and Teams outage hits Australian schools and government services.
author: Guardian World

title: Minister's office warned contractor to settle CFMEU dispute or lose Victorian work, commission hears
content:
A royal commission investigating the integrity of major public and civil infrastructure projects in Victoria heard that a major contractor on a troubled rail project was shut down by union officials. The contractor was warned that the minister’s office said it would not receive any more work in the state unless it resolved the industrial dispute.

The commission also heard testimony from a construction‑company employee who said workers were “fearful” of the union, and, for the first time, from a Victorian Infrastructure Delivery Authority (Vida) official on Friday.
summary: Minister's office warned contractor to settle CFMEU dispute or lose Victorian work, commission hears.
author: Guardian World

title: Joshua Wong sentenced to another 10 years, total over 16 years in prison
content:
A Guardian podcast brings together pro‑democracy activist Nathan Law and journalist Danny Vincent to discuss the latest sentencing of Hong Kong campaigner Joshua Wong. The hosts note that Wong, who has been leading protests since he was 14, has now received an additional ten‑year prison term, taking his total time behind bars to more than sixteen years.  

The episode highlights Wong’s profile as a Time magazine cover subject, the focus of a Netflix documentary and a long‑standing icon of Hong Kong’s pro‑democracy movement, which he has led for the past 15 years. Comments and questions can be sent to tif.Questions@theguardian.com.
summary: Pro-democracy activist Nathan Law and journalist Danny Vincent discuss the sentencing of Hong Kong campaigner Joshua Wong to an additional 10‑year prison term. Wong, who has led protests since he was 14 and has appeared on the cover of Time magazine and in a Netflix documentary, will now serve more than 16 years in prison.
author: Guardian World

title: Defence Secretary Hegseth's group reprimanded at Arlington National Cemetery
content: BBC’s Bernd Debusmann explains that Defence Secretary Hegseth’s group received a reprimand at Arlington National Cemetery on Veterans Day, detailing the incident and outlining the historical basis for the cemetery’s strict rules of conduct.
summary: BBC journalist Bernd Debusmann explains why Defence Secretary Hegseth's group was reprimanded at Arlington National Cemetery. He also outlines the history of the cemetery's strict rules of conduct.
author: BBC World

title: Hunting Alice Bell review: Simon Pegg thriller inspired by Maxine Carr
content:
The drama Hunting Alice Bell is inspired by the story of Maxine Carr and follows a group of women accused of assisting a killer. The series opens with Jason Nash, a murderous anaesthetist portrayed by Simon Pegg, being convicted of aiding and abetting. While a crowd gathers to protest the van transporting a woman to serve an 18-month prison sentence, the individual inside is revealed to be a decoy. The real Alice Bell is smuggled out through a different exit and will receive a new identity upon her release.

The narrative shifts several years later to Fran Da Silva, played by Alexandra Roach, whose life is disrupted when a brick crashes through her window during breakfast with her husband and two teenage stepchildren. Following this incident, Fran faces ostracism at her workplace, while her stepchildren return from school with bloody noses and reports of abuse. At the insistence of social services, the family’s infant daughter is sent to live with her grandmother. The series explores themes ranging from witch hunts to incel culture.
summary: The drama is inspired by the story of Maxine Carr and follows a group of women accused of helping a killer. It features Simon Pegg as a murderous anaesthetist and explores themes ranging from witch hunts to incel culture.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Adam Buxton and Joe Cornish perform 30th anniversary show at Royal Albert Hall
content:
Adam Buxton and Joe Cornish performed a three-hour anniversary show at the Royal Albert Hall, marking thirty years since the debut of their 1990s television series. The duo, who are both 57, recreated their original studio set in the venue for an evening featuring clips, conversation, and music. Their previous show, The Adam and Joe Show, was known for its high-density mix of sketches, pranks, and lo-fi movie parodies that utilized figurines and cuddly toys.

The live performance was described as being as packed with pop-culture references as the original rapid-fire series. The event included a selection of catchy songs and a review of their past work, celebrating the legacy of the show that established them as a cult favorite in the late 1990s.
summary: Adam Buxton and Joe Cornish recreated their 1990s TV show set at the Royal Albert Hall for a three-hour anniversary performance. The event featured pop-culture sketches, pranks, and lo-fi movie parodies using figurines and cuddly toys.
author: Guardian Culture

title: West End theatre audiences embrace cosplay craze for shows like Beetlejuice
content:
A new trend of theatrical cosplay is gaining popularity among West End audiences, with fans dressing in elaborate costumes to match the shows they attend. Critics have noted that this craze involves everything from skeleton suits for Phantom of the Opera to garish wigs for Beetlejuice and themed dresses for Cabaret. The practice has evolved into a significant part of the pre-show experience, transforming traditional theatre queues into colorful displays of fandom.

On Halloween night, the queue outside the Beetlejuice theatre was filled with attendees wearing green wigs, blue face paint, and black-and-white stripes, reflecting the musical’s adaptation of the 1980s film. These theatregoers, who span a wide range of ages, snaked around a corner of the West End in their themed attire. This specific instance highlights how cosplay has become a widespread phenomenon, with fans of all generations engaging in the practice.

The trend extends beyond single productions to include other major West End hits. Queues for different theatres frequently feature fans dressed as characters from Hamilton, Six, and Harry Potter and the Cursed Child. This widespread adoption of costume-wearing is redefining the concept of dressing up for theatre, turning the act into a communal and expressive activity for superfans.
summary: The article describes a growing trend of theatre attendees dressing in elaborate costumes, such as green wigs for Beetlejuice and skeleton suits for Phantom of the Opera. This craze sees fans of various musicals, including Hamilton and Six, adopting themed outfits to enhance their viewing experience.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Diane Morgan's 'Cunk on Cinema' delivers absurd jokes in a three‑part film history
content: This sensationally idiotic guide to film history is hilarious. From a crude Mary Poppins gag to confusing the hell out of Michael Bay, I could listen to Cunk’s surreal tosh all day In a world of slow-burn, jargon-littered dramas, there’s something to be said for the TV programme that sets out its stall within the first 12 seconds. Cunk on Cinema is one such programme. The latest series from Diane Morgan’s sensationally idiotic documentarian is a three-part history of film that begins with our host reeling off some of humanity’s greatest achievements in her deadpan Bolton tones. Specifically, “conquering the landscape, growing the great wall of Chinese, discovering Mona Lisa and inventing global warming”. If you think that list is funny, you’ll enjoy what is essentially a vehicle for some of the stupidest jokes ever written. If you find that kind of malapropism and misapprehension childish, I suggest you switch off immediately. We first encountered Philomena Cunk in 2012 as a spoof talking head on Charlie Brooker’s annual end-of-year Screenwipe special. Billed variously as a “computer typist”, “Bake Off viewer” and “influential Tweetist”, she was at heart a stubbornly ill-informed woman-of-the-people who offered confused commentary on pressing subjects of the time, such as Jimmy Carr’s tax avoidance and the dog from The Artist. Thanks mainly to Morgan’s ability to spout surreal tosh in an appealing no-nonsense fashion, Cunk was a hit. Soon she branched out into solo documentary-making (with Brooker and his longtime colleagues, including Joel Morris and Jason Hazeley, still co-writing her material), covering subjects as modest as “Britain” and later “Earth”, bamboozling her expert interviewees with inane yet dogged questioning like a cross between Jeremy Paxman, Louis Theroux and a far less problematic Ali G.
summary: Cunk on Cinema is a three‑part documentary by Diane Morgan that presents a surreal, humor‑filled history of film. The show begins with Morgan listing absurd achievements and delivers some of the most ridiculous jokes, while her earlier spoof character Philomena Cunk first appeared on Charlie Brooker’s 2012 Screenwipe.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Dan Hicks, NBC Sports broadcaster, dies at 64 after acute illness
content:
Dan Hicks, a sportscaster who served as the voice of golf, Olympic swimming, and Notre Dame football for 35 years at NBC Sports, has died at the age of 64. His death was announced by his family and NBC on Thursday. Hicks passed away late Wednesday in Connecticut.

According to his wife, ESPN broadcaster Hannah Storm, Hicks died of an acute illness.
summary: Dan Hicks, who spent 35 years at NBC Sports covering golf, Olympic swimming, and Notre Dame football, has died at age 64. His wife, ESPN broadcaster Hannah Storm, announced that he died late Wednesday in Connecticut of an acute illness.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Steph Curry defends wife Ayesha against online trolls over on-screen kiss
content:
Steph Curry released a 90-second video on Wednesday from the Instagram account “Wardell Curry” to address online criticism directed at his wife, Ayesha. The four-time NBA champion and Paris Olympic medalist stated that while he and Ayesha are usually unbothered by noise, the current attacks crossed a line by targeting her accomplishments. Curry argued that the critics’ need to offer opinions on matters they do not understand reflects broader societal issues regarding how women are viewed and what they are permitted to do.

The controversy stems from Ayesha Curry’s role as the leading lady in the Christmas romcom Second Chance Holiday. In the film, she portrays a dating expert with bad holiday luck who shares a kiss with a man who is not her husband. According to the source, this on-screen kiss was deemed a bridge too far by some of Curry’s former NBA peers, who had been attacking Ayesha for years.

The article characterizes Curry’s response as a forceful defense that exposes double standards and fragile masculinity within the sports community. It describes the event as a significant moment where fan pressure forced a superstar to publicly defend his wife against what the text labels as an attack on her professional work.
summary: Steph Curry released a video defending his wife Ayesha after online trolls criticized her for kissing another man in a Christmas romcom. Curry stated that attacking his wife's accomplishments reveals broader double standards regarding how women are viewed in the world.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Crystal Palace sack Pierre Sage after five months amid defensive struggles
content:
Crystal Palace has parted ways with manager Pierre Sage after a five-month tenure, a decision driven by a recent losing run and persistent defensive vulnerabilities. The split was prompted by a 1-0 defeat to Liverpool at Selhurst Park, where Alexis Mac Allister scored from a soft free-kick conceded by Jefferson Lerma. This result left the club at the bottom of the table, a position not seen since the start of the 2017-18 season when Frank de Boer was dismissed after five matches.

Chairman Steve Parish, who was visibly distressed during the match, confirmed the managerial change on Thursday. The club, currently in its 14th consecutive top-flight season, faces significant pressure to avoid relegation. This challenge is compounded by ongoing preliminary work on a new £200m main stand, which has raised major doubts regarding funding. With the team struggling with set-piece defenses and a lack of results, Palace is now seeking a new solution to stabilize their position in the league.
summary: Steve Parish cut ties with manager Pierre Sage following a losing run and set-piece struggles that left the club at the bottom of the table. The dismissal comes as Palace seeks a new solution to avoid relegation during their 14th consecutive top-flight season.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Gauff saves three set points to beat Kostyuk at WTA Finals
content:
Coco Gauff defeated Marta Kostyuk 6-4, 7-5 in a round-robin match on Thursday in Indian Wells, California, preserving her chances at the WTA Finals. The American saved three set points during a second-set rally before winning six consecutive games to secure the victory.

Despite the win, the world No. 4 requires assistance to advance to the semi-finals. If fifth-ranked Jessica Pegula defeats Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in the final group match, Pegula will progress instead, as Noskova has already qualified.
summary: Coco Gauff defeated Marta Kostyuk 6-4, 7-5 to keep her WTA Finals hopes alive. Gauff still needs Jessica Pegula to beat Linda Noskova to advance to the semi-finals.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England hand starts to rookies Joseph and Ojomoh for Japan match
content: Only three retained in same positions from Australia game ‘We want the very best of these guys,’ says Maro Itoje England’s World Cup hopefuls have been warned not to go off script when auditioning for a place on the plane next year after Steve Borthwick rang the changes to his side to face Japan on Saturday, handing starts to rookies Will Joseph and Max Ojomoh as well as Henry Pollock. Borthwick has made 10 personnel and two positional changes to his team to play Eddie Jones’s side with a glut of injuries, a handful of players in need of a rest and the head coach’s determination to give those such as Joseph and Ojomoh, who line up on the right wing and inside centre respectively, the chance to shine. Pollock makes his second start, coming in at No 8, while the Northampton scrum-half Archie McParland is in line for a debut from the bench.
summary: Steve Borthwick changed England's lineup for the Japan game, giving starts to rookies Will Joseph and Max Ojomoh and Henry Pollock, while only three players kept their positions from the Australia match. Archie McParland is set to make his debut from the bench.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Arsenal draw with Barcelona in Women's Champions League at Camp Nou
content:
Arsenal secured a draw against European champions Barcelona at the Camp Nou on Thursday night. Frida Maanum scored to put Arsenal ahead, overcoming a dominant performance by the home side. Caroline Graham Hansen later equalized for Barcelona, ensuring the teams shared the points. This result continues Arsenal’s record as a difficult opponent for the European champions.

The match marked Barcelona’s second draw at their main stadium in recent history. The club has won nine matches there, with the other draw occurring against Chelsea in the 2023 semi-finals.
summary: Frida Maanum scored for Arsenal to lead against Barcelona, but Caroline Graham Hansen equalized to secure a draw. Barcelona had previously dominated the match at their home stadium.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Coco Gauff defeats Marta Kostyuk despite back injury to stay in WTA Finals race
content: Coco Gauff overcame a back injury to defeat Marta Kostyuk, preserving her chances of reaching the WTA Finals semifinals. The match highlighted Gauff's resilience as she fought through physical discomfort to secure the victory.
summary: Coco Gauff fought through a back injury to beat Marta Kostyuk. The victory kept her WTA Finals last-four hopes alive.
author: BBC Sport

title: Texas Rep. Chip Roy says GOP focuses on political power over people
content: Texas Rep. Chip Roy (R) criticized the Republican Party on Thursday, arguing that the group is prioritizing “political power” over people. Roy made these remarks following the GOP’s loss of control in both chambers of Congress during last week’s midterm elections. He is scheduled to leave his congressional role on Jan. 3 after an unsuccessful campaign for Texas attorney general.
summary: Texas Rep. Chip Roy criticized the Republican Party for prioritizing political power over the needs of the people. The lawmaker made these remarks after the GOP lost control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections.
author: The Hill

title: Top trade committee Democrats launch probe into Trump administration approving Nvidia’s chip sales to China
content: Senate Finance Committee ranking member Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) and House Ways and Means Committee ranking Democrats announced Thursday that they are requesting the Commerce Department preserve records regarding President Trump’s late-year decision to allow Nvidia to sell H200 chips to China. The top Democrats on the House and Senate trade committees launched this probe into the administration’s approval of the sales.
summary: Top trade committee Democrats launch probe into Trump administration approving Nvidia’s chip sales to China.
author: The Hill

title: FBI: North Korean hackers have stolen $400 million in crypto over last 18 months
content: The FBI said Thursday that North Korean hackers have stolen more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over the past 18 ​months using a social engineering scheme called “FaceStealer.” The scheme uses imposter versions of video conference platforms and secretly recorded web camera videos along with computer intrusions to target people working in the cryptocurrency industry,…
summary: FBI: North Korean hackers have stolen $400 million in crypto over last 18 months.
author: The Hill

title: Kalshi ends Donald Trump Jr. advisory role over Polymarket investment
content: Kalshi has terminated Donald Trump Jr.’s advisory position following his firm, 1789 Capital, increasing its investment in competitor Polymarket earlier this year. Company spokesperson Dani Lever stated that the decision was mutually agreed upon due to the significant investment in a rival platform during the summer.
summary: Kalshi has ended Donald Trump Jr.'s advisory role after his firm, 1789 Capital, increased its investment in Polymarket earlier this year. A company spokesperson stated that the decision was mutually agreed upon following the significant investment in a competitor.
author: The Hill

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after admitting affairs, one with suspected Chinese agent
content: Nvidia’s CEO and co‑founder Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday after admitting an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese agent and a second affair with an Nvidia colleague, an event described as one of Corporate America’s most dramatic scandals in recent years.
summary: Jensen Huang, the CEO and co‑founder of Nvidia, resigned on Thursday after admitting an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese agent. New reporting also links him to a second affair with a Nvidia colleague.
author: The Hill

title: CATL aims for 2,000 battery-swapping stations in China by 2027
content:
CATL, a battery manufacturer, plans to establish 2,000 swapping stations in China by the end of 2027 and intends to introduce the technology to Europe. The company aims to address electric vehicle range anxiety through this battery-swapping infrastructure.

Wang Bing, a 53-year-old driver in Hainan, China, utilizes this system for his daily route between Haikou and Dongfang. He transports approximately five tonnes of goods over a 500-kilometer round trip. Wang, who works eight-hour shifts with a colleague, states that he simply drives into a swapping station to replace his depleted battery with a fully charged one when needed.
summary: Battery maker CATL plans to install 2,000 swapping stations in China by the end of 2027 and bring the technology to Europe. The system allows electric truck drivers to replace low batteries with fully charged ones at dedicated stations.

title: Montenegro herder Mileva Jovanović resists NATO training zone on pastures
content:
The documentary To Hold a Mountain chronicles the life of Mileva “Gara” Jovanović, a herder whose traditional way of life was threatened when her pastures in the Sinjajevina mountains were designated as a NATO training zone. The film, co-written and directed by Biljana Tutorov, highlights Gara’s resilience in the face of this encroachment.

In a recent video call from her winter residence in a village near Podgorica, Gara discussed her daily challenges with her livestock. She noted that her goats frequently escape, requiring constant attention because they are always searching for their paths. Despite these difficulties, Gara expressed confidence in her role, stating, “The goats are good, especially when they know the shepherdess. I’m a good shepherdess. They listen to me.”

Tutorov, who also translated Gara’s Montenegrin into English for the interview, emphasized the stunning nature of the film’s portrayal of life in the mountains. The interview was rescheduled to ensure Gara’s animals were under control before she descended from the peaks to speak with the interviewer.
summary: The documentary To Hold a Mountain follows Mileva “Gara” Jovanović, whose mountain pastures were threatened by plans to become a NATO training zone. Jovanović, who lives in a village near Podgorica, is interviewed about her life as a shepherdess in the Sinjajevina mountains.

title: Tarr Steps bridge faces more frequent storm damage on Exmoor
content:
Tarr Steps, located on Exmoor in Somerset, is the longest clapper bridge in Britain. This ancient footbridge spans nearly 55 metres across the River Barle, featuring 17 arches supported by pillars of piled rock set approximately two metres apart. The structure is held together solely by the bulk and weight of huge, flat gritstones that weigh up to two tonnes each, constructed without mortar, cement, or ironwork. While its exact age is uncertain, the current structure is considered a medieval improvement of a simpler Bronze Age crossing.

The area surrounding the bridge recently experienced fog and cold weather, with a red kite observed overhead. Red kites remain fairly uncommon on Exmoor, although their numbers have increased recently as the species pushes west. Several pheasants were also seen, a species that has become more numerous due to the spread of game-shooting estates. Although Tarr Steps is no stranger to flooding, the frequency of damage from storms is reportedly becoming more and more frequent.
summary: Tarr Steps, the longest clapper bridge in Britain, is experiencing increasingly frequent flood damage. The ancient footbridge is constructed of piled rock and flat gritstones without mortar or cement.

content: Seventeen-year-old Red Cross Society volunteer Isha Rimal was sleeping in Bidur, Nepal, when her house began shaking. Her mother called to inform her of the danger, instructing her to run. The incident occurred during floods that swept through the country following a glacier collapse, an event the source notes is made more likely by climate change.
summary: Isha Rimal, a 17-year-old Red Cross volunteer in Bidur, Nepal, was at home alone when a glacier collapse caused the house to shake. Her mother called to instruct her to run as floods struck the area during the 2026 disaster.

title: Science Tokyo study links sensory nerves to bone recovery after unloading
content:
Researchers from Science Tokyo have identified a critical role for sensory nerves in bone recovery following mechanical loading. Their study on mice demonstrated that sensory nerve abundance fluctuates in response to mechanical unloading and reloading. Notably, removing these nerves prevented bone recovery, highlighting a direct link between mechanical loading, sensory nerves, and the restoration of bone mass.

These findings suggest that sensory nerves are essential for maintaining bone health through mechanical stimulation. The research could pave the way for new sensory nerve-targeted therapies and rehabilitation strategies aimed at treating osteoporosis and fragility.
summary: Researchers from Science Tokyo found that sensory nerves inside bone play a key role in maintaining bone mass and recovering from mechanical unloading. Removing these nerves in mice prevented bone recovery, suggesting potential for nerve-targeted therapies for osteoporosis.

content:

This small plate allows cancer cells, nerves, and blood vessels to grow together, enabling scientists to explore how tumors interact with their surrounding environment.

The findings are detailed in an article published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
summary: On an organ-on-a-chip, researchers can now explore how tumors grow and interact with their surroundings. The chip, a small plate where cancer cells, nerves and blood vessels grow, was developed by researchers at Linköping University, Sweden, in collaboration with colleagues at Politecnico di Milano in Italy.

content: The universe’s dominance by ordinary matter suggests that matter and antimatter are not perfect reflections of each other, though known differences fail to explain the scale of this imbalance. This leaves open the possibility that unknown physics is responsible for the asymmetry. A new analysis of meson decays by the LHCb collaboration has narrowed the scope of the search for such new physics. While the results provide no direct evidence of new phenomena, the study paves the way for more precise measurements in the future.

title: Study links low CO2 and solar radiation to abrupt East Asian monsoon droughts
content:
Researchers from Utrecht University’s Faculty of Geosciences, collaborating with institutes in China and Belgium, have investigated how climate change affects the East Asian monsoon by examining records spanning 250,000 years. Their study, published in Communications Earth & Environment, indicates that over long timescales, the monsoon system tracks variations in incoming solar radiation driven by changes in Earth’s orbit and tilt.

The findings reveal that when solar radiation falls below a specific threshold, abrupt periods of extreme cold and drought occur. These severe climatic shifts are particularly pronounced when atmospheric CO₂ concentrations are low, highlighting a critical interaction between solar input and greenhouse gas levels in driving monsoon variability.
summary: Researchers from Utrecht University and international colleagues analyzed 250,000 years of climate records to investigate East Asian monsoon dynamics. They found that the monsoon tracks solar radiation changes, but abrupt extreme cold and drought occur when radiation falls below a threshold and atmospheric CO2 is low.

title: Distributed Ray Tracer
content:
Julius, a backend engineer at Hatchet, has released a demo of a distributed ray tracer designed to showcase the platform's new durable streams and serverless endpoints. By orchestrating the rendering process across multiple nodes using Hatchet, the system enables the rapid creation of high-fidelity scenes. While the project could be executed on a single machine, the distributed approach allows for faster performance without relying on dedicated hardware such as RT cores.

The renderer employs standard ray tracing techniques and is based on a modified version of the open-source project “rpt” by ekzhang. It includes additional support for Signed Distance Field (SDF) scripting via the “fidget” library. SDFs are a technique popular in the demoscene community that can generate complex visual scenes. A key feature of this implementation is the use of a Domain-Specific Language (DSL) to represent SDFs within the rendering pipeline, allowing users to generate them through an LLM-powered chat interface. The source code for the project is available on GitHub.
summary: Hey HN, I'm Julius, I'm a backend engineer at Hatchet and created this demo to show off some of Hatchet's new features, primarily durable streams and serverless endpoints. Those, however, are just background details that made this significantly easier to scale.

title: Show HN: Cerulion – ROS 2-compatible robotics runtime with multi-process replay
content:
Lakshay and Raveen have introduced Cerulion, a ROS 2-compatible robotics runtime written in Rust, designed to reduce inter-process communication (IPC) transport latencies. The system avoids the tradeoffs of single-process architectures or the restriction to Plain Old Data (POD) message types, which typically prevents the use of standard, vendor-agnostic message types like Image and PointCloud2. Existing ROS 2 nodes and launch files can run unmodified alongside native Cerulion Rust and Python code. The project is available on GitHub, with installation instructions and a quickstart guide provided in the repository README.

The developers cite their experience with off-road autonomy at MIT, where they encountered inter-process latency issues when managing multiple sensors and struggled with debugging non-deterministic callback interleavings. Cerulion addresses these challenges by enabling deterministic resimulation of multi-process graphs. Cerulion bags record per-input reads, scheduler traces, and message content in standard MCAP files. A command-line tool, `cerulion bag play --resim all --verify`, re-executes node code on the recorded schedule to compare outputs for exact matches or defined tolerances, providing specific exit codes to indicate matches, topic divergences, or schedule divergences.

The runtime utilizes a dependency-ordered level-based DAG scheduler with periodic, data, and sync triggers, as well as I/O deadlines and backpressure. By default, each node runs in its own process while preserving deterministic replay capabilities. The system supports ROS 2 versions Foxy, Humble, Jazzy, and Lyrical through the `rmw_cerulion` interface. It also includes features such as `cerulion ros2 attach` to integrate already-running ROS 2 robots and `cerulion ros2 run/launch` to execute existing ROS 2 workspaces without additional setup.

Performance improvements are achieved through iceoryx2 shared memory, which eliminates serialization, payload copying, and payload-sized allocation. This approach supports variable-length messages like sensor_msgs/Image and PointCloud2. The team reports a round-trip latency of 4.08 microseconds at the 50th percentile for a 1MiB sensor_msgs/Image between two processes, compared to 10.95 milliseconds for default ROS 2 Jazzy. This latency remains consistent from 64 bytes to 16 MiB. The system also supports always-on or event-based logging, with a feature called Flashback that maintains approximately 30 seconds of logs and message contents in memory, saving them automatically upon process crashes, topic stalls, or manual triggers.

Additional features include a free account system for pairing robots and desks without IP addresses or discovery chatter, using Iroh for WAN hole-punching or relaying and mDNS over LAN with QUIC. Remote topics are mirrored into local shared memory, with each device having a single network gateway. The platform includes diagnostic tools such as `cerulion doctor` for scanning compile and run-time issues, and Hindsight, an early access MCP for agent-based bag analysis. Cerulion currently runs on Linux (x86_64/ARM64), macOS, and Android (JNI), with more platforms planned.
summary: Show HN: Cerulion – ROS 2-compatible robotics runtime with multi-process replay.

title: Nvidia privately confirms ability to track chips for anti-smuggling measures
content:
Representatives from Nvidia privately informed Illinois Representative Bill Foster that the company could technically implement the anti-smuggling measures mandated by the Chip Security Act. Foster, a Democrat and cosponsor of the legislation, disclosed this information in an interview with MIT Technology Review. The act, introduced in May 2025, seeks to prevent the smuggling of advanced AI chips to China by introducing geotracking requirements to verify chip locations. While the law’s proponents have long claimed the necessary technology exists, Nvidia had not previously confirmed this capability publicly.

This private acknowledgment stands in contrast to public statements made by industry groups. In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, explicitly opposed the bill, characterizing its chip-tracking mandates as “new, untested, and potentially infeasible.” However, during technical discussions with Foster, Nvidia representatives indicated that implementing such safeguards was possible, with one representative reportedly stating, “yeah, of course we can do this.” Foster noted that these assurances were never put in writing, but the company’s private stance goes further than any previous public confirmation.

Evidence suggests Nvidia possesses the technological infrastructure to support such tracking. In December 2025, the company announced a tool called Fleet Intelligence, which allows customers to monitor the performance of advanced chips across various data center locations. Nvidia confirmed to Reuters that this tool can indicate the country in which the chips are located, though the company did not elaborate on whether it could be used specifically to prevent smuggling. When asked directly by MIT Technology Review in early October if Fleet Intelligence could stop the practice, Nvidia declined to answer, instead stating that governments and media have found only “insignificant diversion” of controlled US products.

The legislative push has gained renewed attention following reported controversies involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, including his resignation and an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy. The Chip Security Act is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act. As drafted, the act requires a mechanism to track chip locations through facility inspections, corporate attestations, or ping-based location mechanisms. The ping-based technique, identified by the Center for Security and Emerging Technology in September as the most cost-effective option, would require GPUs to signal their location when they come online.

Foster stated that he did not ask Nvidia’s representatives why the company was not voluntarily adopting these tracking tools despite its technical capability. He acknowledged that if the current bill passes, the tracking mechanisms would only reveal chip locations without providing a method to disconnect smuggled hardware. Consequently, Foster intends to introduce stricter legislation in the new year that would require licenses to operate advanced GPUs, with valid licenses needing verification before a GPU can connect. Foster believes the recent fallout at Nvidia has increased political pressure on companies to ensure accurate geographic validation of chip locations.
summary: Nvidia representatives told Illinois representative Bill Foster that implementing the Chip Security Act's geotracking requirements is technically possible, despite public industry opposition. This private acknowledgment contrasts with the Semiconductor Industry Association's public claim that such mandates are potentially infeasible.

Pricing varies slightly depending on size and color, with most silver and black models in sizes 8 through 13 available at the lowest price point. The newer Oura Ring 5 is described as lighter and thinner than the Ring 4, but it includes the same sensors and software features. author: The Verge

title: Google Faces Calls for AI Moratoriums in Schools After Gemini Pilot Backlash
content: CHICAGO—Families joined protests in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday, rallying against what they see as Google’s bid to entrench its AI models in schools, turn kids of all ages into Gemini guinea pigs, and hook them on AI. The backlash follows a Google statement last week, confirming that there will be no way for students to use Google Search without AI. While Google claimed it was giving schools “more choice, not less”—by turning off Search, Gemini, and Gemini Notebook by default—it would not provide an option that allowed Search without AI. For students, the only way to avoid interacting with AI was to remember to add “-ai” to every query, parents worried. In Chicago, many families showed up to protest Google, despite cold, rainy weather. Waving signs, dozens of protesters marched up to Google’s downtown office as workers seemed to be leaving for the day, shouting chants like “Hey Google, nice try, we don’t want your Gemini” and “Hey, Google, leave our kids alone!” Read full article Comments
summary: Families protested in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday against Google's plan to embed its Gemini AI models in schools. Google confirmed last week that students will not be able to use Google Search without AI, despite claiming it was providing more choice.
author: Ars Technica

title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, replacing Gemini 3.8 Flash
content: Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen. These names are less descriptive than the Pro/Flash monikers of earlier releases, but Hydrogen's purpose is clear: It replaces the faster, more economical Flash models most people in Google's ecosystem use. With Google's recent Argon and Carbon releases, the rollout was staged and began with cybersecurity researchers. Even when general availability began, Google restricted access to users paying for its most expensive AI subscription. The limits for Hydrogen are much more relaxed, with access beginning immediately. This model has replaced Gemini 3.8 Flash across the company's products. Google claims that Hydrogen represents a major improvement versus the previous Flash model. It runs in one of four thinking levels (low, medium, high, and the new xhigh), and even in high mode, it's 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8. Plus, it reduces "fabricated claims" by more than 5x, according to Google's analysis. Users will also see gains in code generation, with Hydrogen more than tripling 3.8 Flash's score in Terminal-Bench. In some cases, Hydrogen even trades blows with Argon. It managed a score of 54 in the popular Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with xhigh mode versus 50 for Argon. Read full article Comments
summary: Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen. These names are less descriptive than the Pro/Flash monikers of earlier releases, but Hydrogen's purpose is clear: It replaces the faster, more economical Flash models most people in Google's ecosystem use.
author: Ars Technica

title: Elder Scrolls Travels: Shadowkey Receives 4K PC Remaster
content:
The Elder Scrolls franchise is adding a long‑forgotten title to its catalog: The Elder Scrolls Travels: Shadowkey is receiving a 4K PC remake. The original game launched in 2004 for the Nokia N‑Gage, a handheld console that offered 176 × 208 pixel resolution and hack‑and‑slash RPG combat.

Shadowkey was one of the few mobile entries in the series, and its low‑resolution graphics and fast‑paced gameplay set it apart from the console and PC releases that followed. The upcoming 4K update will bring the title to modern PC hardware, offering a high‑definition visual experience while preserving the core gameplay that defined the original.
summary: Elder Scrolls Travels: Shadowkey, a 2004 Nokia N‑Gage mobile hack‑and‑slash RPG, is being remastered for PC in 4K resolution. The original game featured 176×208 pixel resolution and is considered one of the franchise's most obscure titles.
author: Ars Technica

title: Drone Attacks on Data Centers Raise Big Tech Security Concerns
content:
Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend has raised new concerns for Big Tech companies, governments, and anyone who relies on common digital services in modern life.

To examine what these attacks mean for society’s reliance on cloud resilience, Ars Live will host a live conversation titled “Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech” on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki.

Joseph Jarnecki is a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts. Jarnecki has researched how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full‑scale Russian invasion, and has explored the implications for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption plans.
summary: Drone Attacks on Data Centers Raise Big Tech Security Concerns.
author: Ars Technica

title: FAA expands AI tool to manage air traffic across US airspace
content:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has announced that it will extend the use of its AI‑driven advisory system, SMART, to all 22 air traffic control centers across the United States. The expansion follows a successful initial deployment in the National Capital Region that began on September 21.

The $875 million SMART system has already rerouted 180 flights in the Washington, DC, airspace. According to FAA data, the system has saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and nearly 80 gallons of fuel per flight. The agency hopes the same efficiencies can be achieved nationwide.

Airline executives have expressed support for the rollout. In contrast, the labor union that represents air traffic controllers stated that it was not involved in designing or testing the AI‑driven system.

In a statement posted on November 10, the FAA said, “After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public.”
summary: The FAA has expanded the $875 million SMART AI system to advise air traffic controllers across all 22 national airspace centers after a successful rollout in the National Capital Region. Airline executives support the rollout, but the air traffic controllers' union said it was not involved in designing or testing the system.
author: Ars Technica

title: American Cancer Society Recommends Routine PSA Screening for All Men
content:
The American Cancer Society has revised its prostate‑cancer screening guidelines, now urging routine PSA testing for all men. The update was released Thursday and marks a shift from previous recommendations that limited routine screening to certain age groups.

Under the new rules, men at average risk should receive a PSA test every two years between ages 50 and 69. Men identified as high risk because of race or family history are advised to begin testing earlier, at age 45, and to have the test annually.

All Black men are specifically recommended to start yearly PSA testing at age 45. Non‑Black men who have a close relative diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or who have more than one relative with the disease, should also begin yearly testing at 45. If a non‑Black man has only one close relative diagnosed at age 65 or older, he should start PSA screening at 45 but can have the test every two years.
summary: In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that all men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA test. Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday.
author: Ars Technica

title: Satellite images show Mauritania fishing port, not migrant fleet bound for Spain
content:
Spain’s Canary Islands have declared a state of emergency as they confront renewed pressure from migrant arrivals. A viral video circulated online asserting that thousands of boats were gathering in Mauritania’s port, allegedly “ready to set sail” to transport migrants to the archipelago.

Satellite imagery examined in the video’s fact‑check shows the scene to be a traditional fishing port rather than a large migrant fleet. The analysis, presented by Vedika Bahl in the “Truth or Fake” segment, concludes that the video’s claim is misleading.
summary: Spain’s Canary Islands have declared a state of emergency amid renewed migrant arrivals. A viral video claimed thousands of Mauritanian boats were ready to sail migrants to the islands, but satellite images show only a traditional fishing port, as explained by Vedika Bahl in Truth or Fake.

She stated that the easiest method for this is to constantly wage a "dirty war" against Europe using illegal and unethical means. These comments address mounting concerns across Europe that recent hoax threats and cyber attacks may be part of a massive hybrid warfare campaign.

The two are pulled into a widening conspiracy that poses an existential threat to a city that’s fighting to be reborn." This engrossing final trailer reveals more of the detailed noir world and Cora's plight to blend into society as a Blade Runner who links up with Olwen, an aging replicant exterminator, for an uneasy partnership. Here, a tense scene plays out in this preview as Cora undergoes an intense police station screening while being used as a resistance pawn to help take back the city from usurping androids. But another deep mystery lies hidden in plain sight! "You have to see the lie that is in front of you," warns Yeoh's dying synthetic cop. Will "Blade Runner 2099" usher in a new era for the sci-fi franchise? (Image credit: Prime Video) " Blade Runner 2099 " sports a spirited cast that includes Dimitri Abold ("The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes") and Lewis Gribben ("Somewhere Boy”) in collaboration with Katelyn Rose Downey ("The Nun II"), Daniel Rigby ('Renegade Nell"), Johnny Harris ("A Gentleman in Moscow"), Amy Lennox ("Only Child"), Sheila Atim ("The Woman King") and Matthew Needham ("House of the Dragon”).
