title: Scotland's Flow Country peatlands become UNESCO World Heritage Site
content:
Scotland’s Flow Country

The Flow Country in northern Scotland consists of extensive blanket bogs—soggy, treeless landscapes dominated by hummocky mosses, grasses and heathers. Ecologists note that these bogs store vast quantities of carbon because their water‑logged soils inhibit microbes from fully decomposing dead plant material. The resulting partially decayed matter builds up as thick, spongy, carbon‑rich peat. Such ecosystems, also referred to as blanket mires or featherbed bogs, develop only where rainfall is abundant, drainage is poor and evapotranspiration is low. Globally, these types of bogs cover about 120,000 square kilometres, less than one‑tenth of one percent of Earth’s land surface.

A Landsat 8 Operational Land Imager (OLI) image captured in spring highlights the Scottish Highlands’ blanket bogs, the largest of their kind in Europe. The photograph, centered on the Flow Country, shows dark‑brown boggy terrain dotted with lakes, light‑green farmland around Thurso on the right, and darker green geometric patterns in the centre that represent conifer plantations. Spring was chosen because the land surface is at its most water‑logged, a period when peat bogs begin to accumulate new biomass.

The Flow Country peatlands, home to more than 30 species of sphagnum moss, span roughly 1,900 square kilometres (730 square miles) of the Highlands. According to UNESCO, some sections have been forming peat for over 9,000 years, producing deposits that exceed eight metres in thickness. While forests store most of their carbon in living trees, peat bogs can retain carbon for many thousands of years.

Scientists estimate that worldwide peatlands cover about 3 percent of Earth’s land surface yet store more than 600 gigatons of carbon—approximately twice the amount stored in all the world’s forests combined. The Flow Country’s peatland has become the first of its type to be inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The image and accompanying story were produced by NASA’s Earth Observatory, with photography by Michala Garrison using U.S. Geological Survey Landsat data and text by Adam Voiland.
summary: The Flow Country in northern Scotland, the largest blanket‑bog ecosystem in Europe, spans about 1,900 km² of the Highlands. It has been designated as the first peatland UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized for its thick peat stores that hold vast amounts of carbon.
author: NASA News

title: APOD November 12 2026: Moon, Venus and Spica appear together over Poland
content: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 12 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Moon, Venus and Spica Meet Explanation: Not all those who wander are lost. A night sky example is that planets wander, and in fact the very word “planet” comes from “wandering star” in Greek. As planets shift relative to fixed stars, they may appear from our perspective to get closer to other astronomical objects. Such meetings are called conjunctions. They don’t happen by chance, but follow the precise laws of celestial mechanics. This peaceful image, captured in Poland, shows the crescent Moon above the Tatra Mountains, and bright Venus close by, a little lower in the horizon. The bright star to the left of Venus is Spica in the constellation of Virgo, the Maiden. Spica is one of the brightest stars in the sky, only about 250 light-years away. It was found in 1890 that Spica is a binary star: two massive blue stars orbiting each other every 4 days. But earlier this year it was reported that Spica, the current companion of wandering Venus, is actually a triple system. Tomorrow’s picture: what’s next? Date November 12, 2026 Credit & Copyright Włodzimierz Bubak Authors & editors: Cecilia Chirenti, Robert Nemiroff, Jerry Bonnell, Keighley Rockcliffe A service of: ASD at NASA / GSFC, NASA Science Activation & Michigan Tech. U. Random APOD Generator Yesterday’s Image APOD: 2026 November 11 – NGC 4449: Small Galaxy, Big Impact Tomorrow’s Image
summary: The November 12, 2026 Astronomy Picture of the Day shows a crescent Moon above Poland’s Tatra Mountains with bright Venus near the horizon and the star Spica to its left. The image notes that Spica, about 250 light‑years away, is now reported to be a triple star system.
author: NASA News

title: Police watchdog warns facial recognition errors risk wrongful arrests of ethnic minorities
content:
Police officers may risk arresting innocent people, especially from ethnic minorities, if they treat inaccurate facial‑recognition data as evidence, an official report warned. Inspectors found that some officers acted on potential matches from retrospective searches without conducting sufficient checks.

The report also noted that while facial‑recognition technology can aid crime‑fighting efforts, it is plagued by errors and biases. Operators often do not realise they must carry out further inquiries to verify the data before using it in investigations.
summary: Inspectors found some officers acted on potential matches from retrospective facial recognition searches without making enough checks. The report says police risk arresting innocent people, especially ethnic minorities, if they treat inaccurate facial recognition data as evidence, noting the technology has errors, biases, and operators often fail to verify the data.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Nvidia board meets to consider ousting CEO Jensen Huang amid stock plunge
content:
Nvidia’s board of directors met on Wednesday to decide whether to oust CEO Jensen Huang, following a week of turmoil. The meeting came after Huang admitted to having a relationship with a woman who is alleged to be a Chinese spy. Earlier on Sunday, the board had expressed confidence in Huang and his leadership team, but the recent revelations have shifted its stance.

Huang’s position became more precarious after the New York Times reported that he had a separate extramarital affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s president of healthcare. Powell was reportedly captured on video being affectionate with Huang at a hotel during a company conference in March. The board’s Wednesday meeting reflects the company’s reassessment of Huang’s leadership amid these disclosures.
summary: Nvidia’s board met on Wednesday to decide whether to remove CEO Jensen Huang as the company’s stock price plunged. The discussion follows reports that Huang admitted a romantic relationship with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy and that he had an extramarital affair with employee Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s president of healthcare.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Nvidia board considers Jensen Huang's future amid reports of second affair
content: Nvidia’s board is reportedly weighing CEO Jensen Huang’s future amid emerging reports of a second affair. The claim follows Huang’s own admission that he has been in a relationship with Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore‑based data‑centre company Megaspeed.
summary: The Nvidia board is weighing Jensen Huang’s future as reports of a second affair emerge. Huang previously admitted a relationship with Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore‑based data centre company Megaspeed.

title: Soldier tells Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and advisers to be silent at Tomb
content: A soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in Arlington instructed US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and his group to maintain silence and respect. The instruction came after the group took photos and were heard laughing.
summary: A soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in Arlington told US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and his advisers to maintain silence and respect. The reprimand followed the group taking photos and being heard laughing.

title: Four survivors rescued after three‑storey Brooklyn building partially collapses, two dead
content:
A three‑storey building in Brooklyn partially collapsed shortly after 4 pm on Wednesday, 11 November, killing at least two people and injuring 17 others.  

Rescuers pulled four survivors from the rubble while firefighters continued to search for additional people feared trapped beneath the wreckage.
summary: At least two people died and 17 were injured when a three‑storey building partially collapsed in Brooklyn shortly after 4 pm on Wednesday, 11 November. Rescuers pulled four survivors from the rubble as firefighters continued searching for others who may be trapped.
author: Euronews

title: Pope Leo XIV welcomed by millions as he begins final stage of tour in Lima
content: The Holy Father starts in Lima the final stage of his Latin American tour: a six-day visit to the country where he served for decades, reaffirming his bond with Peru and urging just healing of past wounds.
summary: Pope Leo XIV was welcomed by millions as he arrived in Lima to begin the final stage of his Latin American tour. During the six‑day visit to the country where he served for decades, he reaffirmed his bond with Peru and called for just healing of past wounds.

title: Pope Leo XIV welcomed in Peru on 11 November, greeted by President Keiko Fujimori
content:
Pope Leo XIV received a rapturous welcome in Peru on 11 November, where he spent more than two decades as a missionary and bishop.  

Greeted by President Keiko Fujimori, he described his return as a homecoming.
summary: Pope Leo XIV received a rapturous welcome in Peru on 11 November, where he spent more than two decades as a missionary and bishop. He was greeted by President Keiko Fujimori and described his return as a homecoming.

title: Zelensky says Ukraine faces systematic restrictions on Starshield satellite network
content: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine has faced systematic restrictions to the Starshield satellite network, which is essential for downing Russian drones, along the entire front line and in occupied areas in recent days. Ukraine’s contract with SpaceX for the network expires next year. Follow our liveblog for updates.
summary: Ukraine has faced systematic restrictions to Starshield, the military satellite network crucial to downing Russian drones, along the whole front line and in occupied areas in recent days, President Volodymyr Zelensky said. Ukraine's contract with the US-based SpaceX service for accessing the network expires next year.

title: Paraguay Central Bank partially refunds eligible Ueno Bank depositors
content: Paraguay's Central Bank announced Wednesday that it had partially returned savings to all eligible depositors of Ueno Bank after the lender collapsed last week. The collapse sparked mass protests and resulted in the impeachment and arrest of former president Santiago Peña, who is accused of directing government funds to the bank.
summary: Paraguay's Central Bank announced it had partially returned savings to all eligible Ueno Bank depositors after the lender collapsed last week. The crisis sparked mass protests and resulted in the impeachment and arrest of former president Santiago Peña, who is accused of directing government funds to the bank.

title: Nvidia board considers firing CEO Jensen Huang after spy affair reports
content: Nvidia’s board convened late Wednesday to discuss the possible removal of chief executive Jensen Huang. The meeting followed reports of two extramarital affairs—one involving an alleged Chinese spy—that triggered a market sell‑off and prompted scrutiny of the AI chipmaker’s leadership.

title: Trappes suspect Kévin Tessier says he acted “on behalf of France” in deadly racist attack
content: In police custody, Kévin Tessier, the main suspect of the October 23 racist terror attack in Trappes, said he was acting "on behalf of France" when he went on a deadly rampage that killed one and left five injured. Investigators also found a sticky note at his home where he had listed names and phone numbers of left-wing figures.
summary: Kévin Tessier, the main suspect of the October 23 racist terror attack in Trappes, said while in police custody that he acted “on behalf of France” during the rampage that killed one person and injured five. title: John Lough: Kremlin recruits poorer, marginalised Russians as expendable cannon fodder
content:
Erin Ogunkeye introduced John Lough, a Senior Research Fellow and Head of Foreign Policy & International Partnerships at the New Eurasian Strategies Centre (NEST Centre) and an Associate Fellow with the Russia & Eurasia Programme at Chatham House. Lough provided an analysis of the social and strategic factors that sustain Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

According to Lough, the Kremlin has recruited a disproportionate share of soldiers from poorer and politically marginalised communities, including regions populated by ethnic minorities. He contends that these groups are targeted because the human cost of their participation is less likely to provoke organised opposition. Lough described many of these recruits as being selected deliberately as “expendable” lives, likening them to “cannon fodder” in the conflict.
summary: John Lough: Kremlin recruits poorer, marginalised Russians as expendable cannon fodder.
author: France 24

content: Nvidia’s board convened late Wednesday to consider removing CEO Jensen Huang, according to a source who spoke to Reuters. The meeting comes as the company, described as the world’s dominant AI‑chip supplier, faces fallout from reports of two extramarital affairs involving its longtime leader. The story was reported by Jack Pownall and Eliza Herbert.

title: China says US fabricated Nvidia spy claims to justify tech blockade
content: China on Thursday accused the United States of “fabricating spy narratives” to justify a technology “blockade”, stepping up its pushback against reports that the woman Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with was a Chinese intelligence asset.
summary: China on Thursday accused the United States of fabricating spy narratives to justify a technology blockade. The accusation followed China's pushback against reports that the woman Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with was a Chinese intelligence asset.

content: Ukrainian ⁠President Volodymyr Zelensky ​on Thursday said that Ukrainian ​military units had recorded new and significant disruptions to the Starshield satellite communications service in recent days, affecting ​the ‌entire front ⁠line and Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine.

title: Iranian officials say Trump may plan new military strike or tighter sanctions
content: Iranian officials, citing adviser Mehdi Mohammadi to chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, say senior Tehran figures believe the United States under President Trump is preparing either additional military strikes or increasingly tight economic sanctions. They warn that a continued stalemate could compel Iran to launch pre‑emptive or retaliatory actions.
summary: Senior Iranian officials, including adviser Mehdi Mohammadi, say the United States under President Trump is planning either additional military strikes or tighter economic sanctions. They warn that a continued stalemate could force Tehran to launch pre‑emptive or retaliatory actions.
author: Guardian World

title: Oil slicks visible from space after missile and mine strikes on tankers in Strait of Hormuz
content:
Since the US‑Iran war began in February, the Strait of Hormuz has seen hundreds of oil spills, creating a “generational” threat to wildlife.  Vast, dark slicks are now visible from space, marking the extent of the contamination.  

Throughout October, oil tankers in the waterway were struck by missiles or sea mines, spilling crude into the sea.  The resulting pollution has spread across the Gulf, contaminating coastlines and threatening lasting damage to marine ecosystems that host dolphins, sea turtles and countless fish species.  

Eight months into the conflict, one of the world’s busiest oil shipping routes has become a battlefield and the centre of a growing environmental disaster.
summary: Since the US war on Iran began in February, oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz have been hit by missiles or sea mines, causing hundreds of oil spills that are visible from space. The resulting slicks have spread across the Gulf, contaminating coastlines and threatening marine life such as dolphins, sea turtles and fish.
author: Guardian World

title: Zelensky says Ukraine faces significant Starshield disruptions as US envoys meet Putin
content: Ukraine’s president said unwelcome ‘speed restrictions’ on military connectivity are ‘helping the Russians kill’ Meanwhile, over in Dublin, Ireland’s Micheál Martin has stressed the need to have a “clear, coherent” European voice in the Ukraine talks, as he answered reporters’ questions ahead of today’s meeting of the European Political Community in Dublin. He said that the issue of Europe’s representation in any talks on Ukraine will be discussed “in the margins” today, with a more formal discussion at the EU informal summit tomorrow. “Obviously, Europe will want a voice at that table, particularly in so far as issued impact on Europe, because of the economic inputs, the security inputs, and in terms of Ukraine’s membership of the EU.” “I think the objective of tonight’s meeting is to debrief president Zelenskyy on the engagement by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner with president Putin, and it’s a moving situation. Our view up to now has been that Russia hasn’t shown any genuine interest in a peaceful resolution of this conflict. It remains to be seen whether that has changed or not.”
summary: President Zelensky said Ukraine is experiencing significant Starshield disruptions and speed restrictions on military connectivity that he says are helping Russians kill. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with President Putin while European leaders, including Ireland's Micheál Martin, discussed Europe's role in Ukraine talks.
author: Guardian World

title: 17-year-old in critical condition after falling from train on Sydney Harbour Bridge
content: ‘You just don’t mess or play with a 400-tonne train’, Sydney Trains says as 17-year-old suffers multiple injuries to head, chest and pelvis Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast A 17-year-old boy is in a critical condition after falling from the outside of a train on the Sydney Harbour Bridge while he was likely train surfing, NSW police say. Around 11.30am on Thursday, emergency services were called to the railway corridor between Wynyard and Milsons Point train stations following reports someone had fallen from a northbound Tangara train onto the tracks on the bridge.
summary: 17-year-old in critical condition after falling from train on Sydney Harbour Bridge.
author: Guardian World

title: Minister Amanda Rishworth launches AI adoption guide after Qantas, Canva cuts
content:
Workplace relations minister Amanda Rishworth has launched a best‑practice guide for employers on adopting artificial intelligence after recent workforce reductions at Qantas and Canva. The guide follows those companies’ restructures, which were described as being driven by AI‑related changes.

The government warned that AI is likely to automate entry‑level positions first. According to the minister, this could result in either fewer working hours and higher wages for ordinary workers, or it could increase burnout and workplace surveillance. Rishworth said employers must provide employees with a clear plan about how automation may affect their jobs and offer pathways to move into new roles.
summary: Minister Amanda Rishworth launches AI adoption guide after Qantas, Canva cuts.
author: Guardian World

title: Mother reunites with 17-year-old son found after six days missing in Victorian bushland
content:
A teenager named William, 17, was reported missing after straying from his camp near Walhalla in Victoria’s Gippsland region. Police AirWing located him lying in a creek close to Walhalla, about 185 km east of Melbourne, on Thursday morning. The discovery came after he had been lost for nearly a week, six days according to his mother’s statement.

Following the rescue, William was reunited with his mother in an emotional meeting, during which she said he would never leave the house again.
summary: William, 17, was reported missing after straying from his camp near Walhalla in Victoria’s Gippsland region. Police AirWing found William, 17, laying down in a creek near Walhalla on Thursday morning, and he was reunited with his mother in an emotional reunion.
author: Guardian World

title: US intelligence says former exec Alice Huang recruited by Beijing to spy on Nvidia
content:
A Thursday briefing notes that U.S. intelligence agencies have assessed the former tech executive known as Alice Huang to be an asset recruited by Chinese intelligence services. The assessment links her to Beijing’s espionage efforts and raises concerns about the security of the artificial‑intelligence sector, as well as about former President Donald Trump’s close relationship with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang.

The briefing describes Alice Huang as a “mysterious Shanghai executive” who developed a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia, one of the United States’ most influential technology companies. U.S. intelligence officials have stated that Alice Huang is not related to Jensen Huang, and that they believe she is acting on behalf of Beijing to gather information for China.

The newsletter promises to detail what is currently known about the case and to examine what the episode suggests about the effectiveness of Chinese espionage operations. It frames the story as part of a broader discussion of potential vulnerabilities in the AI industry and the implications of personal ties between high‑profile tech leaders and foreign intelligence actors.
summary: US intelligence believes former tech executive Alice Huang was recruited by Beijing to spy on behalf of Chinese intelligence services. Huang, who formed a romantic relationship with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, has no familial relation to him.
author: Guardian World

title: Ukrainians face blackouts as Russian attacks hit power grid
content: Ukrainians are confronting widespread blackouts after Russian attacks on the country’s power grid, leaving many without light, water or heat. In parts of Ukraine, parents report that having only a few hours of electricity each day is straining attempts to maintain a normal family routine.
summary: Parents in parts of Ukraine have only a few hours of power each day. The limited electricity results from Russian strikes on the Ukrainian power grid.
author: BBC World

title: League One clubs seek further spending curbs as wage bills rise 15%
content:
League One clubs are seeking additional spending restrictions to curb rising losses and limit owner investment. This move follows a 15% increase in wage bills within the third tier this season. The division previously voted to tighten rules last summer, reducing spending limits from 60% to 50% of turnover and eliminating a staggered approach to owner investment. Under those changes, only 50% of equity injections can be spent on squad costs, with the remainder assigned to infrastructure projects.

Despite these recent adjustments, many clubs want to implement further measures less than six months later. Proposed options under consideration include a luxury tax and three-year limits on losses. These initiatives aim to reduce financial deficits by placing stricter boundaries on how owners can invest in their teams.
summary: League One clubs are considering a luxury tax and three-year loss limits to reduce financial losses from owner investment. This push follows a previous vote to lower spending caps to 50% of turnover and restrict owner equity injections to squad costs.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Thomas Tuchel confirms no release clause in England contract ahead of Euro 2028
content: Head coach did not insert release clause into contract Tuchel ‘open to everything’ including staying after Euros Thomas Tuchel will not be going anywhere before Euro 2028. Mauricio Pochettino is expected to leave his role as the USA men’s head coach to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United, but Tuchel has not lost his passion for international football and has revealed he did not insert a release clause when he extended his deal as England’s manager this year. It will not matter whether there is an approach from a big club before the next tournament. United can pay about £7m to get Pochettino out of his deal, but the Football Association does not have to worry about being forced to let Tuchel go. “There’s no intention [of leaving],” Tuchel said. “I signed the contract. I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business.”
summary: Thomas Tuchel revealed he did not insert a release clause into his extended contract as England's manager. He stated he intends to stay through Euro 2028 to address unfinished business with the team.
author: Guardian Sport

title: NFL trade deadline winners and losers: Vikings go full dadcore with Kirk Cousins in Super Bowl quest
content:
The Minnesota Vikings addressed their offensive struggles following a dispiriting loss to the Buffalo Bills, where quarterback Carson Wentz completed eight of 25 passes for 81 yards, no touchdowns, two interceptions, and a passer rating of 8.9. This performance marked one of the worst in recent history and continued a trend of quarterback futility for the team, which has also involved JJ McCarthy and Kyler Murray. While the Vikings’ defense remains elite, ranking first in scoring defense by allowing 116 points, the team sits 27th in points scored with 146.

Defensive coordinator Brian Flores has been out-scheming other coaches with a variety of blitzes and coverages, but opposing offenses are increasingly able to wait out the defense due to a lack of offensive production. The article notes that teams with championship aspirations have improved their chances at the trade deadline, with the Vikings making a move to support their Super Bowl quest.
summary: Teams with championship aspirations tooled up at the deadline. Most, but not all of them, have improved their chances After what happened Monday night, the Minnesota Vikings had to do this.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Stephen Curry defends wife Ayesha after ex-athletes criticize her movie role
content:
Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry criticized former professional athletes for questioning his wife Ayesha Curry’s role in the romantic comedy Second Chance Holiday. The four-time NBA champion posted a 90-second video on Instagram on Wednesday, responding to comments made by former NBA players Gilbert Arenas and Nick Young, as well as former NFL players Emmanuel Acho and LeSean McCoy. Curry accused the group of diminishing Ayesha’s accomplishments and perpetuating double standards regarding women.

The dispute arose after the release of Ayesha Curry’s new film, which features an on-screen kiss. According to reports, Arenas referred to Ayesha as the “only blemish” on the Curry family. Curry’s response condemned this treatment, highlighting what he described as the inconsistent application of standards when women’s professional choices are scrutinized.
summary: Stephen Curry posted an Instagram video criticizing former athletes for questioning his wife Ayesha's role in the film Second Chance Holiday. He accused them of diminishing her accomplishments and perpetuating double standards regarding women.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pat Cummins urged to end ball‑tampering saga with full disclosure of players' knowledge
content:
Australia’s current Test captain, Pat Cummins, is now facing a “shit sandwich” of his own, according to Geoff Lemon.  The criticism comes from Usman Khawaja’s book, which details how the 2018 Australian team’s ball‑tampering experiments during their South Africa tour were widely accepted by players.  The book also explains that, in March 2018, Cricket Australia blamed Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft for the scandal, while Khawaja’s recent revelations suggest Smith took the fall to protect others.  

Lemon argues that Cummins can end the saga by fully disclosing what the former team members knew, rather than hiding what they did not.  He notes that Khawaja was able to finish his playing career before the revelations, whereas active players such as Cummins, Smith, Mitchell Marsh, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon have not enjoyed that luxury.  The article concludes that the continued secrecy and lack of full truth‑telling have kept the ball‑tampering controversy alive.
summary: Current Test captain Pat Cummins has been handed a criticism in the form of Usman Khawaja’s book, which details the 2018 Australian team’s widespread acceptance of ball tampering. The article says only a full disclosure of what players knew, rather than what they didn’t, could finally resolve the ongoing saga.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pochettino may be appointed Manchester United manager
content:
Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly on the verge of being appointed as the manager of Manchester United. The author notes that this potential appointment is not surprising, as the club has spent the last 13 years cycling through managers with similar structural challenges. Additionally, it is mentioned that the previous eight years have been defined by a near-miss situation regarding Pochettino’s tenure at the club.

The article suggests that Pochettino’s past experiences at elite clubs have left him hurt, yet several players currently at Old Trafford may align with his playing style. The writer describes the situation as a "meat grinder" and implies that Pochettino may have needed to be sufficiently "broken" for the role to fit. There is also a suggestion of an accidental synergy between the manager and the club, despite the history of repeated managerial changes.
summary: Manchester United may be on the verge of appointing Mauricio Pochettino as their manager. The article notes that United have spent 13 years hiring and firing the same structurally doomed manager.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Tyson Fury's journey to heavyweight world champion
content: Tyson Fury, inspired by his father John and drawn to boxing from a young age, became a heavyweight world champion. BBC Sport examines the defining moments that shaped one of Britain's most extraordinary sporting journeys.
summary: Tyson Fury was inspired by his father John and drawn to boxing from a young age. He went on to become a heavyweight world champion in one of Britain's most extraordinary sporting journeys.
author: BBC Sport

title: England Cancel West Indies Test for Home Ashes Warm-ups
content: England has cancelled its scheduled Test match in the West Indies this April. The team will instead prepare for the Women's Ashes by playing red-ball matches domestically in the UK.
summary: England has canceled its scheduled Test match in the West Indies for April. The team will instead prepare for the Women's Ashes with red-ball matches in the UK.

content: Arsenal have contacted Bournemouth regarding midfielder Alex Scott, according to Thursday's transfer gossip. The report also notes that Manchester United have added two defenders to their list of potential targets, while Aston Villa are considering a move for Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia.
summary: Arsenal have made contact with Bournemouth regarding a potential move for midfielder Alex Scott. Other reported transfer news includes Manchester United adding two defenders to their target list and Aston Villa considering a bid for Chelsea's Romeo Lavia.

title: Colom extends slim lead over Hyde-Smith in Mississippi Senate race
content: Democrat Scott Colom has extended his lead in the Mississippi Senate race against Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R) by nearly 4,500 votes, or about half a percentage point. This update follows the counting of absentee and affidavit ballots in Hinds County, a heavily Democratic area. The Associated Press has called the race for Colom.
summary: Democrat Scott Colom has increased his lead in the Mississippi Senate race to nearly 4,500 votes over Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R). The updated count reflects the completion of absentee and affidavit ballot counting in heavily Democratic Hinds County.

content: Democrat Scott Colom is set to become Mississippi’s next senator after Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith conceded Wednesday, notching a major victory for his party in the ruby red state. “While this is not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters,” she said in a video posted to…
summary: Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith conceded the Mississippi Senate race to Democrat Scott Colom on Wednesday. This result marks a major victory for the Democratic party in the state.
