title: Rep. Gregory Murphy concedes North Carolina House race to Democrat Raymond Smith
content: Rep. Gregory Murphy (R-N. C.) conceded his reelection race Wednesday to Democrat Raymond Smith, flipping another House seat for Democrats after a close contest in North Carolina’s 3rd Congressional District a week after the midterm elections.
summary: Rep. Gregory Murphy concedes North Carolina House race to Democrat Raymond Smith.
author: The Hill

title: Dembo says Hegseth impeachment premature after failed House vote
content: Rep.-elect Zach Dembo (D-Ky.), a former Navy JAG who recently flipped a Kentucky House seat, stated Wednesday that it is “premature” to discuss the impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. This comment followed a failed House vote to remove the Pentagon head. Dembo noted he was elected only a week ago and does not yet have an office, adding that he did not arrive with a specific goal regarding the matter.
summary: Dembo says Hegseth impeachment premature after failed House vote.
author: The Hill

title: Hawley urges Senate to pass data center construction moratorium
content: Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) has called on the Senate to enact a moratorium on data center construction before Republicans lose their majority, becoming the first GOP senator to make this nationwide request. In a post on the social platform X, the Missouri senator outlined five priorities for his party, with the data center pause included among them.
summary: Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) is calling on the Senate to pass a moratorium on data center construction in the period before Republicans lose the majority, the first GOP senator to call for the move nationwide.
author: The Hill

title: GOP senator feels ‘strongly’ Jensen Huang should resign at Nvidia
content: Sen. Kevin Cramer (R-N. D.) stated he feels “strongly” that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang should resign. This comment followed reports alleging Huang had an “intimate relationship” with an accused Chinese spy and another with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. Cramer remarked, “I can’t believe we are even considering him not resigning.”
summary: GOP senator feels ‘strongly’ Jensen Huang should resign at Nvidia.
author: The Hill

title: House Republicans select Jim Jordan as minority leader
content: House Republicans have selected Jim Jordan as their next minority leader. Jordan is described as a conservative firebrand and one of Trump’s most vocal defenders.
summary: Jim Jordan has been chosen as the House Republicans' next minority leader. He is a conservative firebrand and one of Trump's most vocal defenders.
author: NPR Politics

title: Ballet dancers exhibit distinct brain responses to others' facial emotions
content: New research from the Centre for Cognition and Neuroscience at City St George’s, University of London reports that ballet dancers exhibit distinct brain responses when viewing other people’s facial emotions. The findings suggest that dance training can shape how individuals perceive both movement and everyday emotional expressions.
summary: Ballet dancers show distinct brain responses to other people's facial emotions. Research from the Centre for Cognition and Neuroscience at City St George's, University of London indicates that dance training can influence perception of everyday emotional expressions.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Experts urge caution over drug company campaigns to destigmatize obesity
content: Experts in The BMJ urge caution regarding pharmaceutical campaigns aimed at destigmatizing obesity. Michael Viggars and colleagues acknowledge that destigmatization is beneficial but warn that companies profiting from obesity treatments may improperly influence public discourse and national policy.
summary: Experts in The BMJ warn that pharmaceutical companies may influence public conversation and national policy through obesity destigmatization campaigns. Michael Viggars and colleagues argue that while destigmatizing obesity is correct, there is a risk of corporate influence given their profits from treatment.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Trial: Pausing blood pressure meds on surgery day reduces low blood pressure in older adults
content: A trial of older adults, published in The BMJ, found that pausing the usual dose of blood pressure medication on the day of surgery reduces the rate of very low blood pressure requiring treatment during the operation compared with taking the medication as normal. The researchers state that this simple strategy provides high-certainty evidence supporting the omission of the morning dose in this population.
summary: A trial published by The BMJ found that pausing blood pressure medication on the day of surgery reduces the rate of very low blood pressure in older adults. The researchers state this strategy provides high-certainty evidence supporting the omission of the morning dose.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Penn State researchers use infrared imaging to study nerve habituation
content:
Losing hand sensation complicates daily tasks such as cooking, driving, and texting. While electrical procedures can substitute for or aid nerve function, their effectiveness often declines over time as the brain adjusts to artificial stimulation, a process called habituation.

Researchers led by a Penn State engineer are employing advanced imaging techniques to investigate the mechanics of this habituation. The team aims to identify optimized treatment settings that could mitigate these issues for patients recovering from strokes or amputations.
summary: A team led by a Penn State engineer is using advanced imaging techniques to understand the mechanics of habituation in electrical nerve treatments. This research aims to find optimized treatment settings to help patients with strokes or amputations who experience reduced effectiveness over time.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Christchurch mutation may protect against Parkinson's and Lewy body dementia
content: Researchers at Oregon Health & Science University suggest that a rare genetic mutation may protect against developing Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia.
summary: A new study from Oregon Health & Science University suggests that a rare genetic mutation may protect against developing Parkinson's disease. The mutation is also linked to protection against Lewy body dementia.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Fluorescent probes reveal fluid-like barriers inside nuclear pores of living human cells
content:
Researchers from Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, the Max Planck Institute for Biophysics in Frankfurt am Main, and Wuhan University in China have used fluorescent probes to investigate transport mechanisms within nuclear pores of living human cells. While the scaffold structure of these pores is well established, the specific process by which molecules traverse them has remained a subject of significant scientific debate.

The study addresses how molecules pass through the several thousand nuclear pores that puncture the double membrane protecting genetic material in the nucleus. The collaborative team’s work sheds new light on this long-standing question regarding intracellular transport.
summary: Researchers from Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, the Max Planck Institute for Biophysics, and Wuhan University used fluorescent probes to study nuclear pores in living human cells. Their work sheds light on how transport takes place within these structures, which are well-known for their scaffold but debated for their internal mechanisms.
author: Phys.org

title: Clean water, hidden risks: New technology reveals neurotoxicity missed by conventional water quality monitoring
content: The provided text uses an orchestra analogy to illustrate that conventional water quality monitoring may fail to detect subtle neurotoxicity, even when standard parameters appear normal. It compares this limitation to a photograph showing musicians present but unable to reveal if they are playing in harmony, suggesting that hidden risks exist despite intact physical appearances.
summary: A photograph of an orchestra can tell you whether the musicians are on stage and their instruments are intact. But it cannot tell you whether they are playing in harmony.
author: Phys.org

title: CSIRO team validates 2019 M87* black hole image with new technique
content: A team of four scientists from CSIRO, Australia’s national science agency, has developed a new imaging technique that validates the landmark 2019 image of the black hole at the center of galaxy M87. This image, produced by the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) collaboration involving hundreds of scientists, captured the first direct view of a black hole’s shadow and has become one of the most recognized scientific images of the modern era.
summary: A CSIRO team of four scientists developed a new imaging technique that validated the 2019 Event Horizon Telescope image of the black hole at the center of galaxy M87. The technique confirmed the first direct view of a black hole's shadow captured by the EHT.
author: Phys.org

title: Ampelomyces Parasite of Powdery Mildew More Common Than Thought
content:
A new study from North Carolina State University has shown that Ampelomyces, an intracellular fungus that attacks the plant disease powdery mildew, is far more common than previously believed.  

Researchers examined museum specimens of powdery mildew that date back roughly 150 years. Their screening revealed that Ampelomyces is widespread in these samples and that many specimens previously labeled as Ampelomyces were actually misidentified. The findings underscore that even parasites can be parasitized, adding complexity to fungal interactions.
summary: A North Carolina State University study found that the intracellular fungus Ampelomyces, which infects powdery mildew, is far more common than previously thought. The study also revealed that many museum specimens labeled as Ampelomyces were misidentified.
author: Phys.org

title: Study maps genetic landscape of bovine TB across Wales
content: A new study has mapped the genetic landscape of bovine tuberculosis across Wales, revealing that the disease is evolving in distinct ways in different regions. As the most detailed analysis of the bacterium to date, it underscores bovine TB as a major animal‑health challenge that impacts cattle health, farm businesses, and exerts significant emotional, social, and financial pressures on farming communities.
summary: The study shows bovine tuberculosis is evolving differently in various Welsh regions. Bovine TB poses significant health, economic, emotional, social, and financial challenges to cattle and farming communities.
author: Phys.org

title: Microplastics detected in blood of wild mammals over 40 miles from human infrastructure
content: A new study published in Nature reports that microplastic particles have been detected in the blood of wild mammals living more than 40 miles from any human infrastructure. The research confirms that higher environmental exposure to these tiny plastics translates into greater accumulation within individual animals. Scientists note that, as with humans, animals are ingesting increasing amounts of microplastics, which have been shown to be hazardous to many species under experimental conditions and are suspected to pose a threat to wildlife in natural settings. The findings provide the first direct evidence linking terrestrial exposure to internal contamination in wild mammals.
summary: Microplastics have been found in the blood of wild mammals more than 40 miles away from human infrastructure. A new paper in Nature confirms that higher environmental exposure translates into higher microplastic accumulation in individual animals.
author: Phys.org

title: SS United States to become world's largest artificial reef
content:
The SS United States, noted for being larger than the RMS Titanic and faster than the RMS Queen Mary, served as the United States’ premier luxury ocean liner in the mid‑20th century, carrying presidents and Hollywood elite across the Atlantic.  

The vessel is now slated to become the world’s largest artificial reef, marking its transition from a celebrated passenger ship to a significant marine habitat.
summary: The SS United States, a mid‑20th‑century luxury ocean liner that once ferried presidents and Hollywood elite across the Atlantic, was larger than the RMS Titanic and faster than the RMS Queen Mary. It is set to become the world's largest artificial reef.
author: Phys.org

title: Only half of England's young workers outside higher education secure permanent contracts, down from 81%
content: A study of young people in England reveals declining job security for those not pursuing higher education. Among this group, only 16% secured apprenticeships and 23% had stable work by ages 19–20. Of those employed, just half held permanent contracts, a significant drop from 81% in a comparable study conducted six years ago.
summary: The study of young people in England found that among those who did not progress to higher education, only 16% secured apprenticeships and just 23% had secured stable work by ages 19–20. Of those in work, only half had a permanent contract, down from 81% in a similar study six years ago.
author: Phys.org

title: Pomerado turns websites into self-healing MCPs for AI agents
content:
Alan and Akshay from Pomerado, a YC F26 startup, have launched a self-serve platform designed to connect AI agents to any website by converting sites into deterministic, self-healing APIs. The founders state that agents are currently limited not by their intelligence, but by their ability to interact with systems that lack APIs or Model Context Protocols (MCPs). They note that airlines, banks, e-commerce platforms, insurance portals, government sites, and legacy portals commonly lack these interfaces, forcing agents to rely on slow, expensive, and unreliable browser automation or computer use. Additionally, the founders mention that many companies have banned computer use due to security and compliance concerns.

The development of Pomerado began when the founders attempted to use personal assistants for daily tasks, such as booking flights, and found that the agents fell back on computer use, which failed during checkout. They identified that just-in-time tool creation could address bottlenecks in legacy verticals, drawing on their previous experience at McKinsey and Scale AI where agent deployments in healthcare, professional services, and telecom were hindered by poor interfaces with legacy websites.

The platform allows users or their coding agents to create APIs for any website, including those they do not own, in minutes. By providing a short natural language description and answering questions about their workflow, users receive an MCP in less than an hour. Future tool calls utilize this deterministic MCP, which typically returns results in five to 30 seconds. The process involves an agent opening a browser to explore the site and perform a task once using HTTP requests or a Playwright script. A separate Guardian model reviews the coding agent’s calls against guardrails, and a battery of tests with synthetic inputs ensures the API is generalized. A final publication agent ensures the integration publishes a reasonable input/output schema.

Pomerado also handles sites requiring authentication and two-factor authentication (2FA). For authentication, the system uses a deterministic sign-in process to ensure models and recorders never read customer credentials. Users can store 2FA TOTP seeds or link their account to a Pomerado phone number for autofilled 2FA. If future runs fail, a maintenance job is triggered to repair the tool, fix broken steps such as renamed buttons, add functionality, or implement new guardrails. The founders emphasize that while the initial setup takes slightly longer, the resulting MCPs are deterministic at runtime, making them faster and cheaper than computer use for repeated, high-volume tasks.

The company offers both an open-source MIT version and a free hosted version. Current users include a personal trainer using agents to prepare workouts and message clients, car dealerships connecting Grok Bots to legacy dealer systems like CRMs and ERPs, and personal assistants integrating with various consumer websites. The founders invite users to try the product and share feedback in the comments.
summary: Pomerado is a self-serve platform that converts any website into a deterministic, self-healing API for agents in minutes. The company offers both an open-source version and a free hosted version to help developers connect agents to legacy systems without relying on browser automation.
author: Hacker News

title: United Blocks Personal AI Assistants from Booking Flights
content:
United Airlines has stated that it will not permit personal AI assistants to book flights, citing privacy and regulatory concerns. According to a report by The Wall Street Journal, the airline has not observed many attempts by customers to use AI agents for ticket purchases, a trend consistent with observations from other businesses such as DoorDash.

Despite the low current usage, United is concerned that AI agents could expose customer information or execute unintended purchases. The company also worries that these agents might bypass federal regulations requiring airlines to share specific information with customers, such as attestations that checked bags do not contain explosives. While AI agents remain capable of displaying available United flights, they are prohibited from completing the booking process.
summary: United will not allow personal AI assistants to book its flights, citing privacy and regulatory concerns. The airline worries that agents could expose customer information, enable unintended purchases, and potentially violate federal rules about bag content attestations, though agents can still display flight options.
author: The Verge

title: Home Assistant Launches Connect Aux-2 Multi-Function Box for Non-Smart Devices
content:
Nabu Casa, the commercial arm of the Open Home Foundation, has launched the Home Assistant Connect Aux-2, a multi-function device designed to integrate non-smart devices into smart home systems. The product is part of Home Assistant’s broader initiative to improve user-friendliness. Nathan Edwards of The Verge has tested the device for several days, describing it as useful and easy to set up.

Priced at $69, the Aux-2 is a compact unit roughly the size of a deck of cards. It features 2.4GHz Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Ethernet, USB-A, and USB-C connectivity. The device also includes a digital/analog audio jack and a Grove port for connecting peripherals such as sensors.
summary: The Aux-2 can be many things. Even a hat for your amp!
author: The Verge

title: Nvidia board to consider firing CEO Jensen Huang over alleged affair
content:
Nvidia’s board is reportedly preparing to dismiss CEO Jensen Huang after a New York Times report revealed a second alleged extramarital affair. The claim comes days after Huang publicly admitted to a separate affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, according to The Wall Street Journal.

The new allegation involves an executive who reports to Huang. The Times identified the executive as Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell.

The board is scheduled to meet as soon as today to decide Huang’s future at the company. Nvidia has not yet responded to a request for comment.
summary: Nvidia's board is preparing to dismiss CEO Jensen Huang after a New York Times report of a second alleged extramarital affair with vice president of health care Kimberly Powell. The board will meet today to decide Huang's future, and Nvidia has not yet responded to a Verge request for comment.
author: The Verge

title: Google DeepMind verifies key parts of Signal protocol
content:
Google DeepMind researchers have used an agentic AI system to mathematically prove, or formally verify, several of the key cryptographic guarantees of the Signal protocol. The effort, carried out as a proof‑of‑concept project over just four weeks, demonstrates the ability of DeepMind’s new AI framework, AlphaProof Code, to conduct formal verification of real‑world security protocols.

The verification provides an independent check of the cryptography that underpins major messaging platforms such as the Signal app, Google Messages, and WhatsApp. By confirming that the protocol functions as intended, the work also highlights the potential of AI‑aided formal verification as a tool for ensuring software security.

While the project marks a milestone for both cryptography and AI, experts note that it remains unclear how practical AI‑driven formal verification will be for widespread use or for securing large codebases. Nonetheless, proponents continue to view formal verification as a “holy grail” of software security, using mathematics to guarantee that code is free of critical vulnerabilities.
summary: Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI to mathematically prove key cryptographic guarantees of the Signal protocol. The four‑week proof‑of‑concept project also showcased DeepMind’s AlphaProof Code framework and provided independent validation for the cryptography used by Signal, Google Messages, and WhatsApp.
author: Ars Technica

title: Trump urged US to legalize Kei cars, Toyota announces Scion KEI‑01
content:
President Trump, who is known for a maximalist approach to policy, announced last year that he wanted the U.S. Department of Transportation to allow Japan’s diminutive “Kei” cars to be sold in the United States. Attempts by Ars to obtain more information from the Department of Transportation about a potential influx of these small vehicles have largely been unanswered.  

In recent developments, Toyota has announced that it will revive the Scion brand with the introduction of the KEI‑01 model. The KEI‑01 is a Kei car, a class of vehicles that in Japan are limited by government regulations on size, engine capacity, and power output.  

The article notes that the dominance of large SUVs in the U.S. market has largely resulted from corporate average fuel economy standards that make it less profitable to sell smaller, efficient cars. Kei cars represent an alternative approach, where government restrictions on vehicle dimensions and power encourage the production of compact, low‑output vehicles.
summary: President Trump announced last year that he wanted the Department of Transportation to make Japan’s diminutive “Kei” cars legal in the United States. Toyota announced this week that it will bring back the Scion brand with the KEI‑01.
author: Ars Technica

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces board talks over affair scandal
content:
Nvidia’s board is scheduled to hold urgent discussions regarding the future of founder and CEO Jensen Huang following revelations of an affair with a senior executive. The Wednesday meeting occurs as a scandal intensifies at the $4.2 trillion company, coinciding with Donald Trump’s statement that the FBI is investigating allegations that Huang was romantically involved with an alleged Chinese spy.

According to two people familiar with the matter, Huang had a romantic relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice-president of healthcare. Powell, described as a prominent public figure and an 18-year veteran of the chipmaker, is central to the unfolding situation involving the company’s leadership.
summary: Nvidia’s board will hold urgent talks on Wednesday about founder Jensen Huang’s future after revelations of an affair with executive Kimberly Powell. The meeting comes amid a scandal involving Trump’s claim that the FBI is investigating Huang’s alleged romantic ties to a suspected Chinese spy.
author: Ars Technica

title: Databricks' revised Genie AI agent gives AI Ghodsi unvarnished truth
content: Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi admits that, with 12,000 employees, he cannot know everyone and that staff are unlikely to openly confess mistakes. To obtain candid insights, he relies on Databricks’ newly revised Genie AI agent, which delivers the unvarnished truth.
summary: Databricks has 12,000 employees and AI Ghodsi says he cannot know everyone or expect them to confess problems. He relies on Databricks' newly revised Genie agent to learn about issues.
author: TechCrunch

title: Siri co‑founder backs Helix’s voice ID technology
content: The co‑founder of Siri is backing Helix’s voice‑identification technology. As AI agents such as Instinct and Muse emerge, the industry is urged to reconsider online human identity and to depend more on biometric cues like voice, a role Helix aims to fill.
summary: A co‑founder of Siri has backed Helix for its voice identification technology. The support reflects growing interest in biometric signals like voice as AI agents such as Instinct and Muse prompt the industry to rethink online identity.
author: TechCrunch

title: Jensen Huang accused of affair with Nvidia subordinate
content:
Jensen Huang has faced criticism after admitting an affair with a woman who has been accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent.  

He is now also being accused of a separate affair with a subordinate at Nvidia.
summary: Jensen Huang has been accused of having a separate affair with an Nvidia subordinate. He previously admitted to an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent.
author: TechCrunch

title: Spain: 120,000 demonstrators march in Madrid over housing costs
content:
Around 120,000 demonstrators marched through central Madrid on Wednesday 11 November, marking Spain’s first nationwide general strike since 2012, authorities said.  

The crowd gathered to demand affordable housing and better wages, protesting soaring housing costs and the growing pressure on household budgets.
summary: Around 120,000 demonstrators marched through central Madrid on Wednesday 11 November. The protest was part of Spain's first nationwide general strike since 2012, aimed at addressing soaring housing costs and pressure on household budgets.
author: Euronews

title: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after peaceful housing-costs march, police use projectiles
content:
Clashes erupted in Barcelona after a peaceful march against soaring housing costs. Burning barricades were set up and riot police confronted masked protesters.

Police used projectiles to disperse the demonstrators, and violence spread through the city centre.
summary: Burning barricades and clashes with riot police erupted in Barcelona after a peaceful march against soaring housing costs. Police used projectiles to disperse masked protesters as violence spread through the city centre.
author: Euronews

title: Millions of workers join Spain's first general strike in 14 years over housing
content:
Millions of workers in Spain shut down businesses and public transport on Wednesday, marking the country’s first general strike in 14 years. The action followed a peaceful march in Barcelona that protested soaring rents, property prices and the rising cost of living.  

During the unrest, protesters smashed storefronts, set off small bonfires, burned bins and launched fireworks toward police. The demonstrations come just weeks before snap elections called by Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez. FRANCE 24’s Sarah Morris reports from Madrid.
summary: Millions of workers join Spain's first general strike in 14 years over housing.
author: France 24

title: Tshisekedi Supports New Law Expanding Conditions for DRC Constitutional Referendum
content: A new law expanding the conditions for a constitutional referendum has sparked political tensions in the Democratic Republic of Congo, a development described as paving the way for constitutional change under President Félix Tshisekedi. Meanwhile, Kenya has officially declared the end of its latest Ebola outbreak, and at COP31 environmental advocates warned that waste incineration could lock African cities into costly, polluting infrastructure.
summary: A new law expanding conditions for a constitutional referendum has ignited political tensions in the DRC. Kenya has officially declared the end of its latest Ebola outbreak, while environmental advocates at COP31 warn that waste incineration could lock African cities into expensive and polluting infrastructure.
author: France 24

title: Russia and Ukraine agree to large-scale prisoner swap as Abu Dhabi talks end
content: Kyiv and Moscow agreed to a large‑scale prisoner exchange on the final day of peace talks in Abu Dhabi, though no figure was disclosed. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will separately meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Thursday.
summary: Kyiv and Moscow agreed on a large-scale prisoner exchange on Wednesday as the final day of peace talks in Abu Dhabi ended, without giving a concrete figure. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will meet separately with Russian President Vladimir Putin and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky on Thursday.
author: France 24

title: Gadi Eisenkot introduces bills to overturn Netanyahu policies
content:
The bloc of Israeli prime‑ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot introduced a series of bills at the opening of the legislative session that target Benjamin Netanyahu and his policies. The proposals call for an official government‑led inquiry into the Hamas‑led Oct. 7, 2023 attacks, the establishment of term limits for the prime‑minister position, and the reversal of changes made by the outgoing Netanyahu‑led government that limited the powers of the judiciary.  

France 24’s Sharon Gaffney discusses these developments with Rina Bassist, editor at Al‑Monitor.
summary: The bloc of Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot introduced a series of bills at the start of the legislative session targeting Benjamin Netanyahu and his policies. The proposals call for a government‑led inquiry into the Hamas‑led Oct. 7, 2023 attacks, prime‑minister term limits, and reversal of judiciary‑limiting reforms.
author: France 24

title: Ireland Deploys Largest Security Operation as 50 European Leaders Meet in Dublin
content: Ireland is mounting the largest security operation in its history as around 50 European leaders gather in Dublin this week. The operation follows a wave of hoax bomb threats targeting airlines and media organisations across Europe, with Irish police reporting new incidents on Monday and Tuesday, according to FRANCE 24’s Olivia Bizot.
summary: Ireland has launched its largest security operation in its history as around 50 European leaders gather in Dublin this week. The operation follows a wave of hoax bomb threats targeting airlines and media organisations across Europe, with Irish police reporting new incidents on Monday and Tuesday.
author: France 24

title: Pope Leo XIV Returns to Peru, Welcomed by Thousands
content: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Peru on Wednesday for the final leg of his South American tour, returning to the country where he spent more than two decades as a missionary and bishop. Thousands gathered to welcome him home as “Padre Robert”, with many hoping his visit will bring attention to poverty, crime and political instability.
summary: Pope Leo XIV Returns to Peru, Welcomed by Thousands.
author: France 24

title: Democrat Scott Colom wins historic Senate race in Mississippi
content:
Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Senator Cindy Hyde‑Smith in Mississippi after a final count on Wednesday, becoming the state’s first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction.

His narrow victory adds to the Democrats’ midterm gains as President Donald Trump’s party suffers a series of defeats.
summary: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi after a final count on Wednesday, becoming the state's first Black US senator since Reconstruction. His narrow victory adds to the Democrats' midterm gains as President Donald Trump's party suffers a series of defeats.
author: France 24

title: WHO says ending cholera by 2030 is within reach; brief notes Haiti crisis, US review
content: The World Health Organization announced on Tuesday that ending cholera as a public health threat by 2030 is within reach. It added that every cholera death can be prevented with tools that already exist.
summary: WHO said ending cholera as a public health threat by 2030 is within reach because every cholera death can be prevented with existing tools. The brief also mentions displacement and hunger in Haiti and a rescheduled US human rights review.
author: UN News

title: UN peacekeepers plan exit from Blue Line after 48 years as southern Lebanon stays volatile
content:
After 48 years of patrolling the Blue Line, UN peacekeepers are preparing to leave Lebanon.  

They report that the situation in southern Lebanon remains volatile and extremely difficult for communities trying to rebuild, even though hostilities have significantly decreased after a June agreement involving the United States, Lebanon and Israel.
summary: UN peacekeepers say the situation in southern Lebanon remains volatile and difficult for residents. Their withdrawal follows a June agreement between the United States, Lebanon and Israel that reduced hostilities.
author: UN News

title: UN chief Guterres urges climate justice pact and fossil fuel tax at COP31
content: UN chief António Guterres used a Wednesday session of COP31 in Antalya to call for a new global climate‑justice pact, urging governments to tax fossil‑fuel companies so that nations most affected by the crisis receive support. His appeal arrived while world leaders convened amid ongoing questions about climate finance and the future role of fossil fuels.
summary: UN chief António Guterres called for a new global climate justice agreement at COP31, urging governments to tax fossil fuel companies to aid vulnerable countries. The appeal was made as world leaders gathered in Antalya, where questions remain about climate finance and the future of fossil fuels.
author: UN News

title: UN emergency relief chief Tom Fletcher urges end to Gaza winter aid delays
content: The UN’s Emergency Relief Coordinator, Tom Fletcher, expressed deep concern about the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Gaza, as UN member states and partners have been repeatedly delaying sending their support to the Strip.
summary: UN Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher said the humanitarian situation in Gaza is deteriorating. He warned that UN member states and partners are repeatedly delaying the delivery of winter aid to the Strip.
author: UN News

title: Democrats win US midterms, sparking relief in European capitals amid Trump threats
content: Far-right populists remain insurgent and pro-EU governments are braced for Trump’s betrayal. But the midterms also showed that democracy can fight back • Don’t get This Is Europe delivered to your inbox? Sign up here “Is Maga dead?” asked Margaret, a Guardian reader in Switzerland, in a live Q&A with our correspondents after the seismic US midterm elections. If Margaret’s query expressed a hope that the Democrats’ blue wave could transform Europe’s fortunes after two years of Maga-induced trauma, she was probably not alone. The resounding defeat for Donald Trump’s Republicans and the installation of a Democratic-controlled US Congress has been met with understandable relief in European capitals. In the short term however, the worst for Europe is not over. Trump didn’t need congressional approval, after all, to unleash a trade war on his supposed European allies, threaten to invade Greenland, try to stitch up Ukraine or go to war with Iran, an act that has inflated fuel and food prices disastrously.
summary: Far-right populists remain insurgent and pro-EU governments are braced for Trump’s betrayal. But the midterms also showed that democracy can fight back • Don’t get This Is Europe delivered to your inbox?
author: Guardian World

title: US‑brokered Abu Dhabi talks yield largest prisoner swap but little peace progress
content:
Ukraine and Russia met in Abu Dhabi for a two‑day, US‑brokered dialogue that produced an agreement on what officials called the “largest prisoner exchange” of the war. The talks, the first such US‑mediated session since February, involved senior delegations from both sides but yielded little movement toward a broader peace settlement.

Separately, US envoys are scheduled to travel on Thursday for meetings in Moscow and Dublin with President Vladimir Putin and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The delegations are led by former President Donald Trump’s representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, who say the effort aims to end the nearly‑five‑year conflict.
summary: Russia and Ukraine agreed to the war’s “largest prisoner exchange” at their first US‑brokered talks since February, while broader peace talks made little headway. Senior delegations led by Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff attended the two‑day meeting, and US envoys are set to visit Moscow and Dublin for talks with Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
author: Guardian World

title: Millions join Spain's first general strike in 14 years to protest housing costs
content:
Millions of people across Spain participated in the country’s first general strike in 14 years, forming picket lines in a 24‑hour nationwide stoppage. The strike was singularly called for by tenants’ associations and later backed by workers’ unions, focusing on a pushback against Spain’s deepening housing crisis and soaring housing prices.

The action took place weeks before a national election in which the far right could be catapulted into power, drawing high participation and highlighting public concern over housing costs.
summary: Millions of people across Spain participated in a 24‑hour nationwide general strike, the first in 14 years, to protest soaring housing prices. The strike was called by tenants’ associations and later supported by workers’ unions, occurring weeks before an election in which the far right could gain power.
author: Guardian World

title: Former officer Beau Lamarre-Condon admits tossing Jesse Baird's phone off bridge
content:
A court heard that former police officer Beau Lamarre‑Condon has admitted throwing Jesse Baird’s phone off a bridge in an attempt to destroy evidence that could incriminate him. The officer said he was trying to eliminate material that might link him to the alleged murders.

Lamarre‑Condon is accused of fatally shooting Baird and his new partner, Luke Davies, with his police‑service weapon inside Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024. The case is now proceeding in court.
summary: Beau Lamarre-Condon, a former police officer, admitted in court that he threw Jesse Baird’s phone off a bridge to destroy evidence. He is accused of fatally shooting Baird and Baird’s partner Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.
author: Guardian World

title: Australian states consider suing tobacco firms for up to $50bn in health costs
content:
Australian state governments are considering a proposal that would allow them to sue tobacco companies for billions of dollars in public hospital and healthcare expenses. The plan, devised by a former barrister who previously helped establish the link between secondhand smoke and lung cancer, estimates that states could seek as much as $50 billion in compensation.

The South Australian government has formally requested advice on the proposal, and officials in other states are currently reviewing it. No further action has been confirmed.
summary: Australian state governments could sue tobacco companies for billions in public hospital and healthcare costs under a proposal developed by a former barrister who helped legally establish that secondhand smoke causes lung cancer. The South Australian government is formally seeking advice on the proposal, and other states are reviewing it.
author: Guardian World

title: Police launch homicide probe after adult male torso found in sofa in Lane Cove North
content: New South Wales police have opened a homicide investigation after a human torso was discovered inside a sofa in bushland on Sydney’s lower north shore. The remains, believed to belong to an adult man, were found in Lane Cove North. Police were alerted to the possible human remains at approximately 2:30 p.m. on Wednesday and responded to the location. The investigation is ongoing.
summary: New South Wales police have opened a homicide investigation after a human torso believed to be that of an adult man was discovered inside a sofa in bushland at Lane Cove North on Sydney’s lower north shore. Police were called to the site at about 2.30 pm on Wednesday following reports of human remains.
author: Guardian World

title: Two skulls of enslaved Brazilians repatriated after Harvard eugenics research
content:
Two skulls believed to belong to enslaved Africans or Afro‑Brazilians were returned to Brazil after being used in eugenics studies at Harvard University. The remains, which had been outside Brazil since the 19th century, were flown back by diplomats and welcomed in subdued ceremonies in Salvador and Rio de Janeiro.

One skull was taken about 190 years ago from Salvador, the capital of Bahia, and the other about 160 years ago from Rio de Janeiro. The skull of a man thought to have participated in Brazil’s greatest slave revolt had been used in racist eugenics research at Harvard. Both skulls were repatriated on Wednesday.
summary: Two skulls believed to belong to Africans or Afro‑Brazilians were flown back to Brazil by diplomats. The remains, taken about 190 years ago from Salvador and 160 years ago from Rio de Janeiro, had been used in eugenics studies at Harvard before being returned in ceremonies in both cities.
author: Guardian World

title: SS United States to be sunk off Florida coast as world's largest artificial reef
content: The historic liner SS United States is slated to be sunk off the coast of Florida, where it will become the world’s largest artificial ocean reef. Activists who sought to preserve the ship as a museum were unsuccessful, and the vessel will now serve as a marine habitat.
summary: Activists unsuccessfully fought for the historic liner to be preserved and turned into a museum. It will now become the world's largest artificial ocean reef off the coast of Florida.
author: BBC World

title: Hubble Space Telescope reveals glittering stars with mysterious origins | Space photo of the day for Nov. 11, 2026
content:
The Hubble Space Telescope has captured a new image of Messier 30 (M30), a globular star cluster located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Capricornus. Released by the European Space Agency (ESA) on November 5, the photograph displays thousands of stars in shades of blue, gold, and orange. M30 is a densely packed, roughly spherical collection of stars held together by gravity, typical of globular clusters that contain tens of thousands to millions of stars.

The Milky Way contains at least 150 of these ancient stellar gatherings, with some estimated to be between 11.5 billion and 13.5 billion years old. Given that the universe is approximately 13.8 billion years old, these clusters are nearly as old as the cosmos itself. Astronomers view such globular clusters as cosmic time capsules because their ancient stars preserve chemical clues about the conditions present during their formation, which helps researchers understand the early history of the Milky Way.

The image also highlights a unique aspect of M30’s movement. Observations indicate that M30, along with several other globular clusters, traverses the Milky Way in the opposite direction to the galaxy's rotation. This unusual motion suggests that M30 may not have formed within the Milky Way. Instead, it is possible that the cluster was captured by the galaxy billions of years ago, offering insights into how the Milky Way evolved.
summary: The Hubble Space Telescope has captured a breathtaking view of thousands of stars glittering like cosmic jewels in a dazzling display of blue, gold and orange. But this spectacular scene is far more than just a pretty picture.
author: Space.com

title: NASA launches Gemini 12 with Aldrin and Lovell to test spacewalks for Apollo
content:
On November 11, 1966, NASA launched the Gemini 12 mission, marking the final flight of the agency’s Gemini program. The crew consisted of mission commander James Lovell and Edwin “Buzz” Aldrin, who lifted off from the Kennedy Space Center aboard a Titan launch vehicle. Their Agena target vehicle had been placed into orbit by an Atlas rocket approximately 90 minutes prior to their launch. This mission was designed to validate critical skills for the upcoming Apollo program, specifically focusing on spacewalking and docking maneuvers.

Prior to Gemini 12, astronauts faced difficulties during extravehicular activities due to a lack of sufficient handholds on spacecraft. To address this, NASA implemented changes for the mission, which resulted in Aldrin successfully performing three spacewalks and spending more than five hours working in space without major issues. During these walks, Aldrin installed handrails and utilized foot restraints and other tools that have since become standard for orbital spacewalks. The crew also tested tools and techniques intended for use on the lunar surface.

The mission included a successful docking with the unpiloted Agena booster, which had launched the same day. During the rendezvous, the crew lost radar lock within 74 miles of the target vehicle, prompting Aldrin to use a sextant to assist Lovell in completing the maneuver. The astronauts spent four days in space before returning to Earth on November 15. Upon reentry, they tested a computer-controlled technique that guided them to a landing just three miles from their target location near the recovery ship, USS Wasp, in the Atlantic Ocean approximately 600 miles east of Cape Canaveral.

The success of Gemini 12 established the fundamentals of spacewalking that Apollo astronauts would later employ. Aldrin, a rookie astronaut at the time and the first to earn a Ph.D., trained for his spacewalks in a neutral buoyancy pool in Maryland to simulate weightlessness. NASA officials noted that this underwater training approach became so successful that it remains the primary spacewalk training method used by the United States, Russia, and China. Today, NASA’s Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory in Houston contains mockups of major sections of the International Space Station and holds 6.2 million gallons of water, making it the largest indoor body of water in the world.

Both Aldrin and Lovell continued their careers in the Apollo program following Gemini 12. Aldrin went on to become the second person to walk on the moon during the Apollo 11 mission, while Lovell served as the commander of Apollo 13. The Gemini 12 crew’s departure from the launch pad was marked by signs on their backs denoting “THE END” of the Gemini program, signifying the transition from the two-person Gemini missions to the more complex Apollo lunar landings.
summary: The Gemini 12 mission launched on November 11, 1966, as the final flight of the Gemini program with astronauts Jim Lovell and Buzz Aldrin aboard. Aldrin performed three spacewalks to test new handholds and tools that established fundamentals for future lunar missions.
author: Space.com

title: Finnish Cathedral Plays Sonified Fast Radio Bursts in "The Logos" Installation
content: Fast radio bursts, flashes of energy from faraway galaxies, are invisible to our eyes. However, we can now hear their melody, thanks to a composer who has turned them into sound. Fast radio bursts, or FRBs, are among the most extreme events in the universe, releasing as much energy in a millisecond as the sun puts out in three days and briefly outshining entire galaxies. Since the first FRB was discovered in 2007, astronomers have detected thousands of them; however, exactly how these cosmic flares are launched remains poorly understood. Recent evidence points to at least one burst coming from the environment around a rotating neutron star. Despite their power, FRBs last only a few thousandths of a second before vanishing into space. Catching one takes luck, as a telescope has to be pointed at the right patch of sky at the right moment. That changed with CHIME (the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment) in British Columbia. With a very wide field of view and a supercomputer to process its data, CHIME more than quadrupled the number of known FRBs in its first year of operation alone. Between 2018 and 2023, CHIME recorded 4,539 bursts from 3,641 sources. As pulses of radio waves, our eyes haven't evolved to see FRBs, nor can we hear them as they aren't sound waves. Well, not until now. "Artist and composer Andrew Melchior turned all of the CHIME bursts into sound for "The Logos," an installation that has played daily at Oulu Cathedral in Finland since early April and is scheduled to run through the end of the year. Melchior and Kiyoshi Masui, an associate professor of physics at MIT, "sonified" the bursts, translating data into acoustics so that human ears can hear them. The structure of each real signal is mapped to varying musical pitches and played through 12 loudspeakers spread throughout the cathedral. The result is a range of tones, with distant FRBs humming, rumbling, popping, and whistling. The signals are old by any human measure. According to a description on Melchior's website, the youngest in the work are about 50 million years old, and the oldest are about 8 to 9 billion years old. An animation shows the random appearance of fast radio bursts (FRBs) across the sky (Image credit: NRAO Outreach/T. Jarrett (IPAC/Caltech); B. Saxton, NRAO/AUI/NSF)) Physics also plays a role in what is heard. Each burst arrives with its high frequencies first and sweeps downward, stretched by its journey through intergalactic gas, "and you can hear that dispersion as it falls from the dome," Melchior told Space. Com by email. Since their discovery in 2007, the bursts are also still yielding discoveries. Last month, astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope pinpointed the host galaxy of the most distant FRB yet, one that went off when the universe was only about 3 billion years old. The galaxy, a small, young, star-forming dwarf, was far smaller than expected. That makes it harder to square with the theory that FRBs come from merging neutron stars, researchers say, which would take billions of years to occur. This fits better with a second theory, in which a young, highly magnetic neutron star called a magnetar produces the burst soon after a massive star explodes, according to NASA. An illustration of a magnetar launching a FRB (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) Back on Earth, an upcoming event at Oulu Cathedral offers a more immediate encounter with the bursts. On Nov. 21, 30 singers will stand among the audience and "sing back to the sky in Finnish" while Melchior plays the bursts live from a keyboard, he told Space. Com by email. "The fast flashes will echo as snare-like beats bouncing through the cathedral," Masui said in a previous MIT statement. "It should feel rich and layered, while also revealing something real about how these signals travel across billions of years of cosmic space before reaching Earth."
summary: Fast radio bursts, flashes of energy from faraway galaxies, are invisible to our eyes. However, we can now hear their melody, thanks to a composer who has turned them into sound.
author: Space.com

title: Dua Lipa, Tame Impala, SZA to Headline Coachella 2027
content:
Dua Lipa, SZA, and Tame Impala will headline the 2027 Coachella festival, marking the conclusion of months of speculation regarding the lineup. The California event is scheduled to take place at the Empire Polo Club in Indio on April 9-11 and April 16-18.

Additional performers include Madonna, who will headline the dance tent alongside Zara Larsson. The full lineup also features Robyn, Phoebe Bridgers, Weezer, and Daddy Yankee.
summary: Coachella 2027 will feature headliners Dua Lipa, SZA, and Tame Impala, with Madonna leading the dance tent. The festival is scheduled for April 9-11 and 16-18 at the Empire Polo Club in Indio.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Jimmy Kimmel calls Hegseth press conference 'doozy of a performance'
content: Late-night hosts discussed embattled defense secretary’s defense of himself amid Republican-led effort to oust him Late-night hosts recapped Pete Hegseth ’s press conference amid impeachment articles and Stephen Miller’s first day as White House chief of staff.
summary: Late-night hosts discussed Pete Hegseth's press conference held amid an impeachment effort and Stephen Miller's first day as White House chief of staff. Jimmy Kimmel described Hegseth's performance as a "doozy" during the segment.
author: Guardian Culture

title: M John Harrison, 81, Wins Booker Prize, First Science‑Fiction Author Honored
content: Kazuo Ishiguro, Jeff VanderMeer, Olivia Laing and other writers weigh in on the publishing world’s genre wars As M John Harrison was announced as the Booker prize winner on Monday evening, the 81-year-old looked gobsmacked. Decades into his career, and long overlooked by the mainstream literary establishment, he had just won a prize that has never before rewarded a writer known for science fiction, with a decidedly fantastical book. His fans, many leading authors among them, are thrilled. “For decades it was a standard – and correct – nerd whine to point out that sentence for sentence, book for book, Harrison was one of the greatest writers out there, full stop, but that ‘mainstream’ prizes never reflected that,” says China Miéville, who last week won the Goldsmiths prize with his 1,200-page speculative novel The Rouse. Back in 2002, Miéville wrote that Harrison not having won a Booker by that point proved “the bankruptcy and back-slapping generic snobbery of the literary establishment”. Now, he says: “I am so delighted, for Harrison, and for fiction.”
summary: M John Harrison, an 81‑year‑old writer known for science‑fiction, was announced as the Booker Prize winner on Monday evening. Authors including China Miéville praised the win, noting it confronts the literary establishment’s generic snobbery.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Fifa separates top four teams until semi-finals at 2027 Women’s World Cup
content:
Fifa has confirmed a change to the draw procedure for the 2027 Women’s World Cup, which will separate the top four ranked teams until the semi-finals, provided each wins their group. Spain, the United States, Germany, and England currently hold the top four positions in the world rankings, although the USA and England still need to qualify for the tournament.

The seedings will be determined by the updated rankings released on 7 December, meaning the standings could shift before the official draw. This event is scheduled to take place on 11 December in Rio de Janeiro.
summary: Fifa confirmed that the top four ranked teams will be kept apart until the semi-finals at the 2027 Women’s World Cup if they win their groups. The seedings will be based on the 7 December updated rankings, with the draw taking place on 11 December in Rio de Janeiro.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Jockey Tom O'Brien, Cheltenham winner, dies aged 39
content: O’Brien rode more than 1,000 winners over jumps ‘Tom meant so much to so many people across our sport’ Tom O’Brien, who rode more than 1,000 winners over jumps including five Grade Ones and two at the Cheltenham festival, has died at the age of 39 after being diagnosed with cancer. O’Brien, who retired from race riding in April 2023, had a close association with Philip Hobbs’s stable near Minehead throughout his 20-year career in the saddle and enjoyed his most prestigious Grade One victories aboard Hobbs’s Thyme Hill in the Stayers’ Hurdle at Aintree in April 2021 and the Kauto Star Novice Chase at Kempton in December 2022.
summary: Jockey Tom O'Brien has died at age 39 after being diagnosed with cancer. He rode more than 1,000 winners over jumps, including five Grade Ones and two at the Cheltenham festival.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England start white-ball tour in Perth as Australia focuses on sandpaper incident
content:
England’s white-ball tour of Australia commences in Perth on Friday, marking a return to the site of their recent Ashes defeat. The series consists of three one-day internationals followed by five Twenty20 matches. Although the tour takes place at Optus Stadium, where England suffered a two-day loss to Australia a year prior, the current atmosphere is notably different from the high-stakes tension of the previous summer.

The focus in Australian cricket has shifted away from the visiting team, with local attention reportedly centered on the sandpaper incident. While Brendon McCullum remains the head coach for limited-overs cricket, the article notes that the intense media attention previously directed at England’s “Bazball” strategy has largely dissipated. Consequently, the tourists are not currently the primary story in Australian cricket, as the mood surrounding the team has changed significantly since their last visit.
summary: England's white-ball tour begins in Perth with three one-day internationals followed by five Twenty20s. The article notes that Australia's attention remains on the sandpaper incident rather than the visiting English team.
author: Guardian Sport

title: IRS Complaint Filed Over FIFA Housekeeper Payroll Claims
content:
A complaint has been submitted to the United States Internal Revenue Service requesting an investigation into allegations that a person on the Fifa payroll was privately employed as a housekeeper for Gianni Infantino. The filing seeks to verify these claims, which, if substantiated, could result in Fifa losing its tax-exempt status in the US. The organization currently holds 501(c)(4) status, a designation for entities created to promote community welfare for charitable, educational, or recreational purposes.

In response to the allegations, Fifa stated that Infantino personally pays for any domestic staff. The complaint specifically targets the potential misuse of organizational payroll for private household services, a practice that would conflict with the requirements for maintaining its current tax classification.
summary: IRS Complaint Filed Over FIFA Housekeeper Payroll Claims.
author: Guardian Sport

content: Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) stated he would support Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) for majority leader if Van Hollen decides to run. title: Sentinel at Tomb of Unknown Soldier admonishes Hegseth group for breaking decorum
content: An Army sentinel at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in Arlington National Cemetery loudly admonished a group, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, for breaking decorum during Wednesday’s annual Veterans Day ceremony. Hegseth, accompanied by senior staff, stopped to take photos, prompting the sentinel to yell at the group to maintain proper conduct. Videos of the incident were subsequently shared online.
summary: An Army sentinel at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier loudly admonished a group including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth for breaking decorum. The incident occurred during the annual Veterans Day ceremony when the group stopped to take photos.

content: Rep. Stephen Lynch (D-Mass.) responded to a White House warning on Wednesday, challenging administration lawyers to “Come at me, bro.” The threat was issued after Democrats announced plans to investigate President Trump and his administration. content: Democratic Sen. content: Sen. James Lankford (R-Okla.) stated that the Republican Party will defer to President Trump regarding the next immigration initiative. content: Nine Kennedy family members have joined legal efforts opposing the construction of Trump’s D.C. Arch. The relatives contend the structure would obstruct views and cast shadows over the graves of their ancestors at Arlington National Cemetery.

title: UK state fund to lend £1bn to KKR and RWE for Vanguard windfarms
content:
The UK national wealth fund is set to lend £1 billion towards the Vanguard offshore windfarm projects off the coast of Norfolk. Prime Minister Andy Burnham described the investment as a vote of confidence in building in Britain, noting that the two windfarms require almost £13 billion in debt financing. However, the article questions whether the private equity giant KKR and German utility RWE actually needed state assistance, given their financial strength.

The piece argues that the project does not represent a fresh expression of confidence, as it has been in development since RWE was awarded the contract to build the windfarms in January’s renewables auction.
summary: The UK national wealth fund will provide a £1bn loan toward the Vanguard windfams off the coast of Norfolk, which require almost £13bn in total debt financing. The article notes that the project has been in development since RWE won a renewables auction contract in January.

title: Labour MPs warn against weakening 2030 electric vehicle targets
content: Exclusive: Cutting 2030 goal would be a ‘step backwards’, say MPs, as ministers clash over proposed reductions Labour MPs are urging the government not to weaken its electric vehicle targets as divided cabinet ministers prepare for a crunch meeting on Thursday to thrash out a compromise. Members of the climate and nature crisis caucus (CNCC) say ministers must not water down a legal requirement for carmakers to ensure that 80% of the vehicles they sell in 2030 are electric, saying doing so would be a backward step and “shortsighted”.
summary: Labour MPs urge the government not to weaken the legal requirement for 80% of vehicles sold in 2030 to be electric. They describe cutting this goal as a backward step ahead of a cabinet meeting to resolve ministerial disagreements.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Study links frequent sleep starts to poorer sleep, higher anxiety
content: A new study published in PLOS Mental Health indicates that individuals who frequently experience sleep starts, also known as hypnic jerks, report poorer sleep quality, greater insomnia severity, and higher anxiety levels compared to those who do not. The research was conducted by Tanja Grünberger and Manuel Schabus of Paris Lodron University Salzburg, Austria, along with their colleagues.
summary: A study published in PLOS Mental Health found that people who frequently experience sleep starts report poorer sleep quality and greater insomnia severity. These individuals also reported higher anxiety levels than those who do not experience these phenomena.

title: CHLA researchers identify key pathway in heart lymphatic vessel development
content: Researchers at Children's Hospital Los Angeles have identified molecular signals that guide the development of the heart's lymphatic vessel network. This discovery provides new understanding of how these vessels form normally and how they react to injury.
summary: Researchers at Children's Hospital Los Angeles have uncovered molecular signals that shape the heart's lymphatic vessel network. This discovery offers new insight into the normal formation of these vessels and their response to injury.
